# Placing Orders

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/evm/intent-gateway/placing-orders.mdx

title: Placing Orders
description: How to place same-chain and cross-chain intent orders using the @hyperbridge/sdk IntentGateway class, with detailed fee mechanics and calldata execution.

# Placing Orders

Intent orders let users express what they want — "swap 1000 USDC on Ethereum for 990 USDC on Arbitrum" — and leave the execution to a competitive market of solvers. Users escrow input tokens upfront; solvers compete to fill the output; the best bid wins.

The `IntentGatewayV2` contract handles escrow, fee accounting, and cross-chain settlement. The `@hyperbridge/sdk` `IntentGateway` class wraps the full lifecycle — from encoding and broadcasting the `placeOrder` transaction to polling for solver bids, submitting the winning `UserOperation`, and streaming real-time status updates — into a single async generator.

## Installation

<Tabs items={['npm', 'yarn', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash lineNumbers
npm install @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash lineNumbers
yarn add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash lineNumbers
pnpm add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Setup

The setup differs slightly depending on whether you are placing a same-chain or cross-chain order.

### Bundler Services

A bundler URL is required for the destination chain. Any ERC-4337-compatible bundler works. [Alchemy](https://alchemy.com/account-abstraction) provides bundler support as part of its RPC endpoints (with Account Abstraction enabled):

| Provider | URL format |
|----------|-----------|
| [Alchemy](https://alchemy.com/account-abstraction) | `https://{chain}.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY` |

### Cross-Chain Orders

```typescript lineNumbers title="setup-cross-chain.ts" icon="typescript"
import { EvmChain, IntentsCoprocessor, IntentGateway } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import { createWalletClient, http } from "viem"
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts"

// Source chain — where the user places the order and tokens are escrowed
const sourceChain = await EvmChain.create("YOUR_SOURCE_RPC_URL")

// Destination chain — bundlerUrl is REQUIRED; solvers submit UserOperations via this bundler
const destChain = await EvmChain.create(
  "https://arb-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY",
  "https://arb-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY",
)

// Hyperbridge coprocessor — hosts the order auction and manages solver bids
const coprocessor = await IntentsCoprocessor.connect("wss://nexus.rpc.polytope.technology")

const intentGateway = await IntentGateway.create(sourceChain, destChain, coprocessor)

const account = privateKeyToAccount("0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY")
const walletClient = createWalletClient({
  account,
  transport: http("YOUR_SOURCE_RPC_URL"),
})
```

<Callout type="warn">
The `bundlerUrl` on the destination chain is **required** for cross-chain orders. `IntentGateway` uses it to submit the solver's `UserOperation` to the ERC-4337 bundler on the destination chain. Without it, bid submission will fail at the `BID_SELECTED` stage.
</Callout>

### Same-Chain Orders

For same-chain swaps, source and destination are the same chain. The `bundlerUrl` is still required — the solver fills the order on the same chain via an ERC-4337 `UserOperation`.

```typescript lineNumbers title="setup-same-chain.ts" icon="typescript"
import { EvmChain, IntentsCoprocessor, IntentGateway } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import { createWalletClient, http } from "viem"
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts"

const RPC_URL     = "https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY"
const BUNDLER_URL = "https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_ALCHEMY_KEY"

// Source and destination are the same chain for same-chain swaps
const chain = await EvmChain.create(RPC_URL, BUNDLER_URL)

// Hyperbridge coprocessor — hosts the auction even for same-chain orders
const coprocessor = await IntentsCoprocessor.connect("wss://nexus.rpc.polytope.technology")

// Pass the same chain instance for both source and dest
const intentGateway = await IntentGateway.create(chain, chain, coprocessor)

const account = privateKeyToAccount("0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY")
const walletClient = createWalletClient({
  account,
  transport: http(RPC_URL),
})
```

<Callout type="info">
The ERC-4337 bundler URL is attached to the `EvmChain` instance — via the second argument to `EvmChain.create()` or the `bundlerUrl` field in `EvmChainParams`. `IntentGateway` reads it automatically from `dest.bundlerUrl`.
</Callout>

## How `placeOrder` Works

Understanding what happens on-chain helps you construct orders correctly.

```solidity
function placeOrder(Order calldata order, bytes32 graffiti) external payable;
```

### Data structures

```solidity
struct Order {
    bytes32 user;           // Set by placeOrder to msg.sender
    bytes source;           // Set by placeOrder to current chain ID
    bytes destination;      // Target chain state machine ID
    uint256 deadline;       // Block number deadline for fills
    uint256 nonce;          // Set by placeOrder (auto-incrementing)
    uint256 fees;           // Dispatch fees in fee token
    address session;        // Session key for solver selection (address(0) to disable)
    DispatchInfo predispatch; // Pre-order execution (swap before escrow)
    TokenInfo[] inputs;     // Tokens escrowed from user
    PaymentInfo output;     // What the solver must provide
}

struct TokenInfo {
    bytes32 token;   // Token address as bytes32; bytes32(0) = native token
    uint256 amount;
}

struct PaymentInfo {
    bytes32 beneficiary;  // Recipient of output tokens
    TokenInfo[] assets;   // Output tokens solver must provide
    bytes call;           // Optional calldata executed after fill (via CallDispatcher)
}

struct DispatchInfo {
    TokenInfo[] assets;   // Assets sent to CallDispatcher before order
    bytes call;           // Calldata for pre-order execution
}

```

### Protocol fees

Before escrowing, the contract deducts a protocol fee from each input amount:

```
protocolFee = input.amount × protocolFeeBps / 10_000
reducedAmount = input.amount − protocolFee
```

The fee is retained in the gateway as dust (emitting `DustCollected`). Per-destination fee overrides (`_destinationProtocolFees`) take precedence over the global `_params.protocolFeeBps` when set.

**The commitment hash is computed over the fee-reduced inputs.** Solvers read `reducedAmount` from the `OrderPlaced` event and only need to match those amounts.

### Dispatch fees

`order.fees` is a tip paid to the solver who fills the order. For same-chain orders it compensates the filler for gas; for cross-chain orders it covers the Hyperbridge relayer fees required to deliver the `RedeemEscrow` message back to the source chain. Setting it too low makes the order unattractive to solvers — leave it as `0n` and the SDK will estimate an appropriate amount automatically.

The contract accepts the fee in the ERC-20 fee token (pre-approve and leave `msg.value = 0`) or in native ETH (`msg.value > 0`), in which case the gateway swaps it to the fee token via Uniswap V2 on your behalf. The fee is held against the commitment and released to the solver on a successful fill, or refunded to the user if the order is cancelled.

### Session key

The SDK generates a one-time session keypair per order and sets `order.session` to its public address. The session key authorizes exactly one solver to fill the order via an EIP-712 `SelectSolver` signature. This is handled automatically when you use `IntentGateway.execute()` or `IntentGateway.placeOrder()`.

### Commitment

After fee deduction and field stamping, the order commitment is:

```
commitment = keccak256(abi.encode(order))  // with reduced inputs, filled user/source/nonce
```

The SDK populates `order.id` with this commitment after the `OrderPlaced` event is parsed.

### Graffiti

Every `placeOrder` call accepts an optional `graffiti` field — a `bytes32` tag that identifies the frontend or integration that originated the order. It is passed as calldata and enables on-chain attribution of orderflow to specific integrators for revenue sharing.

Pass your graffiti as the second argument to `executeBest()` / `execute()`. The SDK exports `DEFAULT_GRAFFITI` — a zero `bytes32` — for unattributed orders.

```typescript lineNumbers title="graffiti.ts" icon="typescript"
import { DEFAULT_GRAFFITI } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import { stringToHex, padHex } from "viem"

// Encode your integrator identifier as a right-padded bytes32
const MY_GRAFFITI = padHex(stringToHex("my-app"), { size: 32 })

const gen = intentGateway.executeBest(order, MY_GRAFFITI, {
  auctionTimeMs: 15_000,
})

// Use DEFAULT_GRAFFITI to opt out of attribution
const gen = intentGateway.executeBest(order, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI, { auctionTimeMs: 15_000 })
```

## The `executeBest()` Generator

The SDK exposes two execution entry points:

- **`executeBest()`** — the batteries-included autopilot. It runs the full lifecycle and auto-selects the best bid each round (sort → simulate → sign → submit). Use this when you want the SDK to pick the winning bid for you. This is the recommended starting point and the path documented below.
- **`execute()`** — the consumer-driven variant. Identical placement and auction flow, but instead of auto-selecting it hands you the bids and lets you rank and execute one yourself. See [Custom bid selection with `execute()`](#custom-bid-selection-with-execute) below.

Both share the same signature and the same `IntentOrderStatusUpdate` stream.

`executeBest()` auto-estimates fees, encodes and broadcasts the `placeOrder` transaction, runs a timed auction to collect solver bids, submits the winning `UserOperation`, and streams real-time status updates. During the auction period, the generator yields `NEW_BID` each time a previously unseen bid arrives, giving callers real-time visibility into the auction. After the auction ends, the best bid is selected and submitted. If a round's bids all fail, it keeps polling for fresh bids until the deadline. For same-chain orders it loops back after each partial fill, retrying until the order is fully filled or the deadline is reached.

### Generator protocol

The generator is bidirectional — it pauses at two points to hand control back to the caller:

**First yield** — `AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER`. The generator yields `{ status: "AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER", to, data, value, sessionPrivateKey }`. You sign and submit the transaction, then pass the result back via `gen.next(result)`. The result can be either:
- A **serialized signed transaction** (raw RLP-encoded bytes) — the SDK will broadcast it and wait for confirmation.
- A **transaction hash** (exactly 66 characters: `0x` + 64 hex chars) — the SDK will wait for the receipt of an already-submitted transaction.

**Second yield** — `ORDER_PLACED`. After the transaction is confirmed, the generator yields `{ status: "ORDER_PLACED", order, receipt }` where `order` is the finalized `Order` (with `nonce`, `id`, and `inputs` populated from the `OrderPlaced` event) and `receipt` is the full viem `TransactionReceipt` of the placement transaction.

**Subsequent yields** — status updates. The generator then yields `IntentOrderStatusUpdate` objects continuously until the order reaches a terminal state (`FILLED`, `EXPIRED`). During the auction period (`auctionTimeMs`), the generator yields `NEW_BID` each time a new solver bid is discovered — these are informational and do not affect bid selection. Once the auction ends, `BIDS_RECEIVED` is yielded with the full set of collected `Bid` objects, and `executeBest` selects and submits the best one. `FAILED` events are informational — the executor automatically retries by looping back to bid polling. Call `gen.next()` with no arguments to advance after each update.

```typescript lineNumbers title="executeBest.ts" icon="typescript"
import { IntentOrderStatus, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import type { IntentOrderStatusUpdate, Order } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

async function runOrder(order: Order) {
  const gen = intentGateway.executeBest(order, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI, {
    auctionTimeMs: 15_000, // duration in ms to collect bids before selecting the best one
    pollIntervalMs: 5_000, // how often to poll for new bids during the auction (default: SDK-defined)
  })

  // First yield: AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER — placeOrder calldata + estimated native fee
  const { value: { to, data, value } } = await gen.next()

  // Sign the placeOrder transaction. value covers the fee token swap if paying in native.
  const signedTx = await walletClient.signTransaction({
    to,
    data,
    value,
    type: "eip1559",
  })

  // Second yield: ORDER_PLACED — finalized order (nonce, id, inputs set from OrderPlaced event)
  const { value: { order, receipt } } = await gen.next(signedTx)
  console.log("placeOrder tx:", receipt.transactionHash)
  // store the full order incase you need to cancel it later
  console.log("Order commitment:", order.id)

  // then stream status updates
  for await (const update of gen) {
    switch (update.status) {
      case IntentOrderStatus.AWAITING_BIDS:
        // Auction started — SDK is polling the Hyperbridge coprocessor for solver bids
        console.log("Auction started, waiting for solver bids…")
        break
      case IntentOrderStatus.NEW_BID:
        // A new bid arrived during the auction period (informational — bid selection happens after auction)
        console.log(`New bid during auction`)
        break
      case IntentOrderStatus.BIDS_RECEIVED:
        // Auction ended — all collected bids are available; executeBest picks the best one
        console.log(`Auction ended, ${update.bidCount} bids collected`)
        break
      case IntentOrderStatus.BID_SELECTED:
        // Best bid chosen and UserOp submitted to the ERC-4337 bundler
        // Cross-chain: the generator idles until the deadline — Hyperbridge finalisation is async
        // Same-chain: SDK waits for the fill tx, then moves to FILLED or PARTIAL_FILL
        console.log("Bid selected, solver:", update.selectedSolver, "tx:", update.transactionHash)
        break
      case IntentOrderStatus.PARTIAL_FILL: {
        // Same-chain only: a solver partially filled the output
        // SDK automatically loops back to AWAITING_BIDS for the remaining amount
        const { filledAssets, totalFilledAssets, remainingAssets } = update
        console.log("Partial fill:", filledAssets, "| total filled:", totalFilledAssets, "| remaining:", remainingAssets)
        break
      }
      case IntentOrderStatus.FILLED:
        // Order fully filled; escrow released to the solver
        console.log("Order fully filled! tx:", update.transactionHash)
        return
      case IntentOrderStatus.EXPIRED:
        // Order deadline reached, or no new bids arrived for the remaining amount
        // The order is still live on-chain — cancel it or wait for a solver to fill the rest manually
        console.warn("Order expired:", update.error, "Remaining:", update.remainingAssets)
        return
      case IntentOrderStatus.FAILED:
        // Retryable error (e.g. bundler rejection, simulation failure)
        // The executor automatically retries — this is informational only
        console.warn("Retryable error, retrying:", update.error)
        break
    }
  }
}
```

### Status reference

| Status | Trigger | Key fields |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| `AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER` | Before broadcasting — SDK yields calldata for signing | `to`, `data`, `value`, `sessionPrivateKey` |
| `ORDER_PLACED` | `placeOrder` tx confirmed on-chain | `order` (finalized `Order`), `receipt` |
| `AWAITING_BIDS` | Auction started, polling coprocessor for bids | `commitment`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets` |
| `NEW_BID` | New bid discovered during auction (informational) | `commitment`, `bid` (one `Bid`) |
| `BIDS_RECEIVED` | Auction ended, all bids ready for selection | `commitment`, `bidCount`, `bids` (`Bid[]`) |
| `BID_SELECTED` | Best bid chosen and UserOp sent to bundler | `commitment`, `selectedSolver`, `userOpHash`, `userOp`, `transactionHash` |
| `PARTIAL_FILL` | Same-chain partial fill confirmed; loop restarts | `commitment`, `filledAssets`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets` |
| `FILLED` | Order fully filled | `commitment`, `userOpHash`, `transactionHash` |
| `EXPIRED` | Deadline reached or no new bids available — terminal | `commitment`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets`, `error` |
| `FAILED` | Retryable error (e.g. bundler rejection) — executor retries automatically | `commitment`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets`, `error` |

### Options

Both `executeBest()` and `execute()` take the same options:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `auctionTimeMs` | `number` | — | **Required.** Duration in ms to collect bids before selecting the best one. During this period, `NEW_BID` is yielded each time a new bid is discovered. After the auction ends, `BIDS_RECEIVED` is yielded. |
| `pollIntervalMs` | `number` | SDK default | How frequently (ms) to poll the coprocessor for new bids during and after the auction |
| `maxPriorityFeePerGasBumpPercent` | `number` | `8` | Bump percentage applied to the priority fee estimate during fee estimation |
| `maxFeePerGasBumpPercent` | `number` | `10` | Bump percentage applied to the max fee estimate during fee estimation |
| `solver` | `{ address, timeoutMs }` | — | Restrict bids to `address` until `timeoutMs` elapses, then accept any solver |

## Custom bid selection with `execute()`

`executeBest()` picks the winning bid for you. When you need your own ranking — preferred solvers, reputation, MEV protection, batching the fill with other calls — use `execute()` instead. It is identical to `executeBest()` except at the `BIDS_RECEIVED` stage: instead of auto-selecting, it hands you the collected `Bid` objects and waits for you to execute one and feed the result back.

`execute()` is **bidirectional in two places**: after `AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER` you feed back the signed placement tx (as with `executeBest()`), and after `BIDS_RECEIVED` you feed back the `SelectBidResult` returned by `bid.execute()` (or `undefined` to keep polling for fresh bids).

Each `Bid` exposes:

- `solverAddress`, `outputs`, `relayerFee`, `nativeDispatchFee`, `userOp` — metadata for ranking.
- `simulate()` — pre-check the bid off-chain via `eth_call`; throws if it would revert.
- `execute()` — sign the solver selection and submit the UserOp to the bundler; returns a `SelectBidResult`.
- `outputUsdValue()` — price the bid's outputs in USD (`null` if any token can't be priced).

```typescript lineNumbers title="custom-selection.ts" icon="typescript"
import { IntentOrderStatus, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import type { Order, SelectBidResult, HexString } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

async function runOrder(order: Order) {
  const gen = intentGateway.execute(order, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI, { auctionTimeMs: 15_000 })

  let input: HexString | SelectBidResult | undefined
  while (true) {
    const { value: update, done } = await gen.next(input)
    input = undefined
    if (done) break

    switch (update.status) {
      case IntentOrderStatus.AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER: {
        // Sign + broadcast the placeOrder tx, feed the hash back
        input = await walletClient.sendTransaction({ to: update.to, data: update.data, value: update.value })
        break
      }
      case IntentOrderStatus.BIDS_RECEIVED: {
        // Your selection logic. Here: highest USD output that passes simulation.
        const sorted = await intentGateway.sortBids(order, update.bids)
        for (const bid of sorted) {
          try {
            await bid.simulate()
            input = await bid.execute() // SelectBidResult fed back to the generator
            break
          } catch {
            // bid failed simulation/execution — try the next
          }
        }
        // leaving `input` undefined tells the executor to keep polling for fresh bids
        break
      }
      case IntentOrderStatus.FILLED:
        console.log("Order filled!")
        return
    }
  }
}
```

<Callout type="info">
After an app restart, resume a previously placed order with `resume()` (consumer-driven) or `resumeBest()` (autopilot). They take the same options as `execute()` minus the placement step, and require the order's `id` and `session`.
</Callout>

### `EXPIRED`

When `EXPIRED` fires, the order deadline has been reached or no new bids are available. The user can cancel and reclaim the remaining escrow. See [Cancelling Orders](./cancelling-orders) for cancellation options.

### `FAILED` (retryable)

`FAILED` events are informational — the executor automatically retries by looping back to bid polling. Common causes include bundler gas price rejections or bid simulation failures. The retry continues until the order reaches `FILLED` or `EXPIRED`.

## Same-Chain Orders

Set `destination` to the source chain's state machine ID. The contract verifies `keccak256(source) == keccak256(destination)` and settles atomically on-chain with no cross-chain messaging.

```typescript lineNumbers title="same-chain-order.ts" icon="typescript"
import { toHex, parseUnits } from "viem"

const USDC = "0xYourUsdcAddress" as `0x${string}`

const order: Order = {
  user: "0x",                                                   // set by contract (msg.sender)
  source: "0x",                                                 // set by contract (host().host())
  destination: toHex(sourceChain.config.stateMachineId),           // same as source → same-chain
  deadline: BigInt(await sourceChain.client.getBlockNumber()) + 200n, // ~40 min on Ethereum
  nonce: 0n,                                                    // set by contract (_nonce++)
  fees: 0n,                                                     // auto-estimated by SDK
  session: "0x",                                                // set by SDK (generated keypair)
  predispatch: { assets: [], call: "0x" },
  inputs: [{ token: USDC, amount: parseUnits("1000", 6) }],
  output: {
    beneficiary: account.address,
    assets: [{ token: USDC, amount: parseUnits("990", 6) }],
    call: "0x",
  },
}

await runOrder(order)
```

<Callout type="info">
`TokenInfo.token` and `output.beneficiary` are standard 20-byte EVM addresses (`0x…`). The SDK left-pads them to `bytes32` when encoding the contract call — you do not need to pad them yourself.
</Callout>

### Partial Fills

Same-chain orders support partial fills. Multiple solvers can each fill a portion of the output independently; the contract releases escrowed input tokens proportionally per fill:

```
releasedEscrow[i] = inputs[i].amount × fillAmount / totalRequired
```

The contract emits `PartialFill` for each partial fill and `OrderFilled` only when every output reaches its target. Postdispatch calldata (`output.call`) executes only on full fill, never on partials.

## Cross-Chain Orders

Set `destination` to the target chain's state machine ID. The contract verifies `keccak256(source) != keccak256(destination)` and routes to cross-chain logic.

Cross-chain fills are **all-or-nothing** — the solver must provide the full required amount for every output asset in a single transaction. Partial fills are not supported for cross-chain orders. On fill, the contract dispatches a `RedeemEscrow` POST request via Hyperbridge back to the source chain, which releases escrowed tokens to the solver on receipt.

`execute()` exits after `BID_SELECTED` for cross-chain orders — it does not wait for Hyperbridge finalisation. To track cross-chain settlement, monitor the `EscrowReleased` event on the source chain or use the indexer.

```typescript lineNumbers title="cross-chain-order.ts" icon="typescript"
import { toHex, parseUnits } from "viem"

const USDC_SOURCE = "0xUsdcOnEthereum" as `0x${string}`
const USDC_DEST   = "0xUsdcOnArbitrum" as `0x${string}`

const order: Order = {
  user: "0x",
  source: "0x",
  destination: toHex("EVM-42161"),                     // Arbitrum
  deadline: BigInt(await sourceChain.client.getBlockNumber()) + 200n,
  nonce: 0n,
  fees: 0n,
  session: "0x",
  predispatch: { assets: [], call: "0x" },
  inputs:  [{ token: USDC_SOURCE, amount: parseUnits("1000", 6) }],
  output: {
    beneficiary: account.address,                               // recipient on Arbitrum
    assets: [{ token: USDC_DEST, amount: parseUnits("990", 6) }],
    call: "0x",
  },
}

await runOrder(order)
```

### Surplus sharing

When a solver overpays on a cross-chain fill, the excess is split:

```
protocolShare    = surplus × surplusShareBps / 10_000
beneficiaryShare = surplus − protocolShare
```

If the order has postdispatch calldata, **100% of surplus goes to the protocol** to prevent manipulation of calldata side effects.

## Predispatch Calldata

Predispatch runs arbitrary calls *before* tokens are escrowed. Assets listed in `predispatch.assets` are transferred from the caller to the `CallDispatcher`, the encoded `Call[]` in `predispatch.call` execute against it, and then the contract measures the `CallDispatcher`'s resulting balance for each input token — escrowing exactly `inputs[i].amount` and sweeping any excess as dust.

The canonical use case is **swap-then-escrow**: the user sends WETH, the predispatch call swaps it to USDC via a DEX, and the USDC balance that lands in the `CallDispatcher` becomes the escrowed order input. The user never needs to hold the input token before placing the order.

```solidity
struct Call {
    address to;
    uint256 value;
    bytes data;
}
```

```typescript lineNumbers title="predispatch-order.ts" icon="typescript"
import { toHex, parseEther, parseUnits, parseAbi, encodeAbiParameters, encodeFunctionData } from "viem"
import { IntentGatewayV2ABI } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const WETH        = "0xWethAddress" as `0x${string}`
const USDC        = "0xUsdcAddress" as `0x${string}`
const ROUTER      = "0xUniswapV2Router" as `0x${string}`

// Fetch the CallDispatcher address from the gateway params
const { dispatcher } = await sourceChain.client.readContract({ address: "0xGatewayAddress", abi: IntentGatewayV2ABI, functionName: "params" })

const wethIn      = parseEther("1")
const usdcMin     = parseUnits("2000", 6)
const swapDeadline = BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600)

function encodeCalls(calls: { to: `0x${string}`; value: bigint; data: `0x${string}` }[]) {
  return encodeAbiParameters(
    [{ type: "tuple[]", components: [{ name: "to", type: "address" }, { name: "value", type: "uint256" }, { name: "data", type: "bytes" }] }],
    [calls],
  ) as `0x${string}`
}

const erc20Abi  = parseAbi(["function approve(address,uint256) returns (bool)"])
const routerAbi = parseAbi(["function swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256,uint256,address[],address,uint256) returns (uint256[])"])

// 1. Approve the router to spend WETH from inside the CallDispatcher
const approveData = encodeFunctionData({ abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "approve", args: [ROUTER, wethIn] })
// 2. Swap WETH → USDC; output lands in the CallDispatcher
const swapData    = encodeFunctionData({ abi: routerAbi, functionName: "swapExactTokensForTokens", args: [wethIn, usdcMin, [WETH, USDC], dispatcher, swapDeadline] })

const order: Order = {
  user: "0x",
  source: "0x",
  destination: toHex("EVM-42161"),
  deadline: BigInt(await sourceChain.client.getBlockNumber()) + 200n,
  nonce: 0n,
  fees: 0n,
  session: "0x",
  predispatch: {
    assets: [{ token: WETH, amount: wethIn }],               // transferred to CallDispatcher first
    call: encodeCalls([
      { to: WETH, value: 0n, data: approveData },
      { to: ROUTER, value: 0n, data: swapData },
    ]),
  },
  inputs: [{ token: USDC, amount: usdcMin }],                 // escrowed after the swap
  output: {
    beneficiary: account.address,
    assets: [{ token: USDC, amount: usdcMin }],
    call: "0x",
  },
}

await runOrder(order)
```

<Callout type="warn">
The gateway escrows exactly `inputs[i].amount`. Any USDC left in the `CallDispatcher` above that amount is swept into the gateway as dust and emits `DustCollected`. Size `usdcMin` conservatively to avoid over-escrowing.
</Callout>

## Postdispatch Calldata

Postdispatch runs calls *after* the solver delivers output tokens. Set `output.beneficiary` to the `CallDispatcher` so it receives the tokens, then encode `output.call` with what should happen next.

**Timing differences by order mode:**

| Mode | When postdispatch executes |
|------|---------------------------|
| Same-chain | Only after the order is **fully** filled — partial fills do not trigger it |
| Cross-chain | Immediately after the solver transfers tokens, **before** the `RedeemEscrow` message is dispatched |

After execution, any tokens remaining on the `CallDispatcher` are swept back to the gateway as dust. When `output.call` is non-empty, **100% of any surplus goes to the protocol** — `surplusShareBps` is not applied.

```typescript lineNumbers title="postdispatch-order.ts" icon="typescript"
import { toHex, parseUnits, parseAbi, encodeAbiParameters, encodeFunctionData } from "viem"
import { IntentGatewayV2ABI } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const USDC      = "0xUsdcAddress" as `0x${string}`
const AAVE_POOL = "0xAavePoolAddress" as `0x${string}`
const { dispatcher } = await sourceChain.client.readContract({ address: "0xGatewayAddress", abi: IntentGatewayV2ABI, functionName: "params" })

const outputAmount = parseUnits("990", 6)

function encodeCalls(calls: { to: `0x${string}`; value: bigint; data: `0x${string}` }[]) {
  return encodeAbiParameters(
    [{ type: "tuple[]", components: [{ name: "to", type: "address" }, { name: "value", type: "uint256" }, { name: "data", type: "bytes" }] }],
    [calls],
  ) as `0x${string}`
}

const erc20Abi = parseAbi(["function approve(address,uint256) returns (bool)"])
const aaveAbi  = parseAbi(["function supply(address,uint256,address,uint16)"])

// Approve Aave to pull USDC from the CallDispatcher, then deposit on behalf of the user
const approveData = encodeFunctionData({ abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "approve", args: [AAVE_POOL, outputAmount] })
const supplyData  = encodeFunctionData({ abi: aaveAbi,  functionName: "supply",  args: [USDC, outputAmount, account.address, 0] })

const order: Order = {
  user: "0x",
  source: "0x",
  destination: toHex("EVM-42161"),
  deadline: BigInt(await sourceChain.client.getBlockNumber()) + 200n,
  nonce: 0n,
  fees: 0n,
  session: "0x",
  predispatch: { assets: [], call: "0x" },
  inputs: [{ token: USDC, amount: parseUnits("1000", 6) }],
  output: {
    beneficiary: dispatcher,                                   // CallDispatcher receives output tokens
    assets: [{ token: USDC, amount: outputAmount }],
    call: encodeCalls([
      { to: USDC, value: 0n, data: approveData },
      { to: AAVE_POOL, value: 0n, data: supplyData },
    ]),
  },
}

await runOrder(order)
```

---

# Simplex

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/evm/intent-gateway/simplex.mdx

title: Simplex
description: Simplex is an automated binary that monitors Intent Gateway orders and fills them profitably, earning fees by providing liquidity and execution services.

# Simplex

Simplex is an automated binary that monitors Intent Gateway orders and fills them profitably. It watches configured chains for `OrderPlaced` events, waits for sufficient confirmations based on the order's value, evaluates profitability across all configured strategies, and executes the best fill. Fillers earn the difference between order inputs and outputs.

## Quick Start

### Docker (Recommended)

```bash lineNumbers
docker pull polytopelabs/simplex:latest
docker run --rm -it polytopelabs/simplex:latest --help
```

## Strategies

Simplex ships with two built-in strategies configured as `[[strategies]]` entries in your TOML config. For every order, Simplex evaluates all configured strategies and executes whichever returns the highest profit.

### Stable

The Stable strategy fills cross-chain orders where the input and output token are the same — USDC→USDC or USDT→USDT across chains. It checks your balance on the destination chain, estimates `order fees - (gas + protocol fees + relayer fees)`, and fills directly if profitable.

The `bpsCurve` sets the minimum basis-point margin required at each order size. Points are interpolated, so you can model tighter spreads for larger orders:

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "stable"
bpsCurve = [
    { amount = "100",    value = 100 },   # $100 orders: 1% minimum margin
    { amount = "1000",   value = 50  },   # $1000 orders: 0.5%
    { amount = "10000",  value = 25  },   # $10k orders: 0.25%
    { amount = "100000", value = 10  },   # $100k orders: 0.1%
]
```

The Stable strategy requires pre-positioned stablecoins on each destination chain (optionally backed by the [`[vault]` treasury](#vault-treasury-erc-4626)).

### HyperFX

HyperFX fills swaps between USD-pegged stablecoins (USDC/USDT) and a single configurable exotic token — for example, cNGN (a Nigerian naira stablecoin). It supports both **same-chain** and **cross-chain** orders.

Same-chain orders (`source == destination`) are filled immediately without waiting for additional confirmations. Cross-chain orders use the configured **confirmation policy** for HyperFX to determine how many confirmations to wait for before bidding.

Profit comes from two sources: the **bid/ask spread** on the exotic token, and **order fees** minus gas. The filler holds both stablecoins and the exotic token. When a user swaps stable→exotic the filler sells exotic at the ask price; when the user swaps exotic→stable the filler buys at the bid price. The spread between the two curves is the filler's margin per trade.

Both curves are expressed in **exotic tokens per USD**. A higher bid means the filler acknowledges fewer stables are owed per exotic received (the filler profits more on the exotic→stable leg). A lower ask means the filler sends fewer exotic tokens per stable received (the filler profits more on the stable→exotic leg).

`maxOrderUsd` caps the filler's exposure per order. Orders larger than the cap are partially filled up to that amount — the IntentGateway releases inputs proportionally to the fraction of outputs provided, so partial fills work without any extra on-chain logic.

HyperFX always uses the solver selection path: it submits a signed bid to Hyperbridge via `IntentsCoprocessor` rather than calling `fillOrder` directly. This requires `substratePrivateKey` and `hyperbridgeWsUrl` in `[simplex]`, plus a `bundlerUrl` on each `[[chains]]` entry.

On startup, Simplex automatically delegates the filler's EOA to the `SolverAccount` contract via EIP-7702 — submitting a no-op UserOp through the bundler so the delegation lands without requiring the EOA to hold native gas. Circle Paymaster covers the delegation tx (and subsequent fills) in USDC on chains where it is deployed; on chains without the paymaster (e.g. BSC), Simplex falls back to a direct type-0x04 delegation tx and tops up the ERC-4337 EntryPoint deposit to cover `targetGasUnits` (default 3M) at current gas price.

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000

# Bid price curve: exotic per USD when *buying* exotic from a user (exotic→stable leg).
bidPriceCurve = [
    { amount = "100",  price = "1580" },
    { amount = "1000", price = "1575" },
    { amount = "5000", price = "1570" },
]

# Ask price curve: exotic per USD when *selling* exotic to a user (stable→exotic leg).
askPriceCurve = [
    { amount = "100",  price = "1560" },
    { amount = "1000", price = "1555" },
    { amount = "5000", price = "1550" },
]

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-56"  = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnBsc"
"EVM-137" = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnPolygon"
```

#### One-sided LP

With both curves set HyperFX fills in both directions. Omitting one curve restricts the filler to a single direction, so it keeps accumulating one asset while only giving away the other:

- **Ask only** (omit `bidPriceCurve`) — the filler only *sells* exotic, filling orders where the user sends stable and receives exotic. It accumulates the stablecoin and gives away the exotic token (for example, take USDC, hand out cNGN).
- **Bid only** (omit `askPriceCurve`) — the filler only *buys* exotic, filling orders where the user sends exotic and receives stable. It accumulates the exotic token and gives away the stablecoin.

Orders in the disabled direction are rejected before bidding (an order with mixed-direction legs is rejected as a whole, since the IntentGateway settles all legs atomically).

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000

# Ask curve only — keep accumulating USDC by only selling cNGN
askPriceCurve = [
    { amount = "100",  price = "1560" },
    { amount = "1000", price = "1555" },
    { amount = "5000", price = "1550" },
]

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-56"  = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnBsc"
"EVM-137" = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnPolygon"
```

When pricing from a [Uniswap V4 pool](#pool-based-pricing) (no curves), there is no curve to omit, so set **`side`** on the `[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]` block instead — `"ask"` to only sell exotic (accumulate stablecoins) or `"bid"` to only buy exotic. Omit `side` to fill both directions. `side` cannot be combined with static curves.

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-8453" = "0x46C85152bFe9f96829aA94755D9f915F9B10EF5F"

[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]
side = "ask"  # only sell exotic; keep accumulating stablecoins
positions = [
    { chain = "EVM-8453", tokenId = "2087350" },
]
```

#### Uniswap V4 LP funding

<Callout type="info">
This is the HyperFX-specific **Uniswap V4 LP** funding source, configured per strategy under `[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]`. It funds (and prices) the **exotic** token from concentrated-liquidity positions. It is distinct from the filler-wide [`[vault]` stablecoin treasury](#vault-treasury-erc-4626) (ERC-4626), which is configured at the top level and sources **stablecoins**.
</Callout>

When the solver's wallet balance on the destination chain is insufficient to fill an order, HyperFX can automatically withdraw liquidity from on-chain positions to cover the deficit. Withdrawal calls are prepended to the UserOperation as ERC-7821 batch calls, making the funding atomic with the fill.

Configured under `[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]` within the HyperFX strategy block. Decreases liquidity from concentrated Uniswap V4 positions via PositionManager NFTs. Slippage tolerance is set by `spreadBps` (default 50 bps / 0.50%), deadline defaults to the order's deadline. Only the `tokenId` (the ERC-721 position NFT ID) is required; pool details are read on-chain at startup.

```toml lineNumbers
[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]
positions = [
    { chain = "EVM-8453", tokenId = "123456789" },
]
```

<Callout type="info">
Vaults are initialized at startup; on-demand **refresh** runs before each withdrawal plan so calculations use current on-chain reserves. Simplex can aggregate withdrawals across multiple vaults if needed.
</Callout>

To find your `tokenId`, open your position on the Uniswap V4 app — the token ID is the number in the URL (e.g. `app.uniswap.org/positions/v4/8453/2087350` → `tokenId = "2087350"`).

<figure style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center' }}>

![Uniswap V4 position NFT](/uniswap_nft.svg)

<figcaption>Copy the token ID from your Uniswap V4 NFT position page to use as the <code>tokenId</code> in your vault config.</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Pool-Based Pricing

When **`[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]`** lists at least one position, HyperFX derives bid/ask prices from **Uniswap V4 pool state** (current tick). This is the recommended approach — let the pool act as your price oracle rather than maintaining static curves.

With Uniswap V4 positions configured, you can **omit** `bidPriceCurve` and `askPriceCurve` entirely. The optional **`spreadBps`** field (basis points) sets the slippage tolerance for on-chain LP redemptions. For example, `spreadBps = 50` applies a 0.50% slippage tolerance on remove-liquidity operations. Defaults to `50` if omitted.

Uniswap V4 venue pricing uses pools that pair the exotic token with **USDC or USDT** (addresses from your chain config). When multiple positions exist for the same exotic token on a chain, the most-liquid qualifying pool’s price is used.

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000
spreadBps = 50  # 0.5% slippage tolerance on LP redemptions

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-8453" = "0x46C85152bFe9f96829aA94755D9f915F9B10EF5F"

[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]
positions = [
    { chain = "EVM-8453", tokenId = "2087350" },
]
```

<Callout type="info">
Startup validation requires a pricing source: **either** full static `bidPriceCurve` and `askPriceCurve` (≥2 points each), **or** at least one `[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]` position. Omitting both curves without Uniswap V4 positions fails validation.
</Callout>

#### Uniswap price guards

Pool-based pricing trusts the live pool, which leaves the filler exposed to a manipulated, stale, or thin pool returning a bad quote. To bound that risk, give a position a **`referencePrice`** and **`maxDeviationBps`**. Whenever the pool quote on that chain drifts more than `maxDeviationBps` above or below the reference, the filler refuses to fill — the order is rejected before any bid is submitted.

`referencePrice` is expressed in **exotic tokens per USD**, the same units as the bid/ask curves. The two fields must be set together; omit both to leave the chain unguarded.

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-8453" = "0x46C85152bFe9f96829aA94755D9f915F9B10EF5F"

[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]
positions = [
    # referencePrice is the expected cNGN per USD; reject if the quote is more than 2% off
    { chain = "EVM-8453", tokenId = "2087350", referencePrice = "1575", maxDeviationBps = 200 },
]
```

#### Example profit calculation

For a \$1000 USDC → cNGN order, the curve interpolates to bid 1575, ask 1555 at the $1000 size:

```
User sends:       $1000 USDC
Filler delivers:  1,555,000 cNGN      (1000 × ask 1555)
Filler's cost:    1,555,000 / 1575    = $987.30  (valued at bid)
Spread profit:    $1000 − $987.30     = $12.70
Fee profit:       $2.80 − $1.30 costs = $1.50
Total profit:     ~$14.20
```

## Configuration

### `[simplex]`

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex]
maxConcurrentOrders = 5
logging             = "info"                     # trace | debug | info | warn | error

# Required for HyperFX / solver selection
substratePrivateKey = "0x.."                     # Hex seed or mnemonic for Hyperbridge extrinsics
hyperbridgeWsUrl    = "wss://nexus.rpc.polytope.technology"  # Hyperbridge WebSocket endpoint

[simplex.queue]
maxRechecks    = 10
recheckDelayMs = 30000
```

### Signer Configuration

The `[simplex.signer]` section defines how Simplex signs EVM transactions. Two modes are supported:

The signer is a tagged union — set `type` to select the variant, then add the variant's fields directly under `[simplex.signer]`:

**Private Key** — Signs transactions locally using a raw private key:

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex.signer]
type = "privateKey"
key  = "0x..."
```

**MPC Vault** — Signs transactions via [MPC Vault](https://mpcvault.com), an institutional custody service that uses MPC for signing ceremonies:

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex.signer]
type                          = "mpcVault"
apiToken                      = "your-api-token"
vaultUuid                     = "your-vault-uuid"
accountAddress                = "0xYourWalletAddress"
callbackClientSignerPublicKey = "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."
# grpcTarget = "api.mpcvault.com:443"  # optional, this is the default
```

<Callout type="info">
MPC Vault requires an Ed25519 keypair registered in the MPC Vault console and a running client-signer container (<code>ghcr.io/mpcvault/client-signer:latest</code>). See the <a href="https://docs.mpcvault.com">MPC Vault documentation</a> for setup instructions.
</Callout>

**Turnkey** — Signs transactions via [Turnkey](https://turnkey.com), a key management platform with HD wallet support. Create a wallet in the Turnkey Dashboard and use `signWith` to reference your existing Ethereum address:

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex.signer]
type             = "turnkey"
organizationId   = "your-org-id"
apiPublicKey     = "your-api-public-key"
apiPrivateKey    = "your-api-private-key"
signWith         = "0xYourWalletAddress"
```

<Callout type="info">
Create an API keypair in the Turnkey Dashboard under user details. The <code>signWith</code> field is any Ethereum address from your Turnkey wallet. See the <a href="https://docs.turnkey.com">Turnkey documentation</a> for setup instructions.
</Callout>

### Delegation & Gas Payment

Solver selection requires each filler's EOA to be delegated to the `SolverAccount` contract. Simplex performs this automatically at startup via EIP-7702:

- **Primary path** — builds a no-op UserOperation with an attached EIP-7702 authorization and submits it through the configured bundler. When the Circle Paymaster is deployed on the chain and the filler holds ≥1 USDC, the paymaster pays gas in USDC (EIP-2612 permit) so the filler never needs native gas for delegation.
- **Fallback** — if the bundler path fails or the chain has no paymaster (e.g. BSC), Simplex sends a direct type-0x04 delegation tx using the filler's native balance. On these chains it also keeps the ERC-4337 EntryPoint deposit topped up to cover `targetGasUnits` (default 3,000,000) at the current gas price.

No manual steps are required — delegation is idempotent and skipped if the EOA is already delegated to the correct contract.

### Overfill Protection

Bounds per-leg loss if the filler's internal pricing is wrong (bug, stale cache, manipulated venue). For every order, the filler clamps its computed output to at most `(1 + maxOverfillBps) × user-requested amount` — this ceiling applies to every strategy. After `maxConsecutiveClamps` consecutive orders where the clamp activated, the **HyperFX** strategy halts itself — a pattern that strongly suggests a systemic pricing error — and requires an operator restart. HyperFX additionally rejects any order where the total output USD value ≥ total input USD value.

Defaults are sensible (`maxOverfillBps = 500` ≈ 5% ceiling, `maxConsecutiveClamps = 3`). Override under `[simplex.overfillProtection]`:

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex.overfillProtection]
maxOverfillBps       = 500   # 5% ceiling above user-requested output
maxConsecutiveClamps = 3     # halt threshold (HyperFX)
```

### Vault treasury (ERC-4626)

The optional top-level `[vault]` section configures a **filler-wide stablecoin treasury** backed by ERC-4626 vaults. Any ERC-4626 vault works — for example Aave's `stataToken` for USDC — so idle treasury earns yield while remaining available for fills. Only the vault address is required; the underlying asset and its decimals are resolved on-chain at startup.

<Callout type="info">
This is distinct from the HyperFX-specific [`[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]`](#uniswap-v4-lp-funding) source. `[vault]` is filler-wide and sources **stablecoins** (the input/output token of the Stable strategy); `[strategies.vault.uniswapV4]` is per-strategy and sources/prices the **exotic** token.
</Callout>

One vault list drives three behaviours:

1. **Sourcing** — when wallet balance is short on a fill, Simplex withdraws the deficit from the solver's vault position. The withdrawal is prepended to the UserOperation as ERC-7821 batch calls, so it is atomic with the fill.
2. **Sweeping** — a timer (`sweepIntervalMs`, default 5 min) waits for wallet balance to reach the `threshold` high-water mark, then deposits everything down to `minBalance`. Size `minBalance` to cover working fill float plus gas/paymaster spend; the `threshold`–`minBalance` gap is the guaranteed minimum sweep size, so balance oscillates between the two without thrashing on dust.
3. **Shutdown** — on stop, positions are kept across restarts by default. Set `redeemOnShutdown = true` on a vault to instead redeem its position back to the underlying asset when the filler stops.

Omit `threshold`/`minBalance` on a vault to make it **withdraw-only** (sourcing + shutdown, no sweeping) for that token.

```toml lineNumbers
[vault]
sweepIntervalMs = 300000   # optional, default 5 min
vaults = [
    # Aave stataUSDC on Base — once balance hits $5,000, sweep down to $3,000
    { chain = "EVM-8453",  vault = "0xC768c589647798a6EE01A91FdE98EF2ed046DBD6", threshold = "5000", minBalance = "3000" },
    # Aave stataUSDT on Arbitrum
    { chain = "EVM-42161", vault = "0xa6D12574eFB239FC1D2099732bd8b5dC6306897F", threshold = "5000", minBalance = "3000" },
]
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chain` | yes | State-machine ID the vault lives on (e.g. `"EVM-8453"`) |
| `vault` | yes | ERC-4626 vault address |
| `threshold` | no | High-water balance (human units) that triggers a sweep down to `minBalance`. Omit to disable sweeping (withdraw-only). |
| `minBalance` | conditional | Wallet floor (human units) the sweep deposits down to. Required when `threshold` is set, and must be less than it. |
| `redeemOnShutdown` | no | Redeem this position back to the underlying asset on shutdown. Defaults to `false` (the position is kept across restarts). |

### Rebalancing

The optional `[rebalancing]` section keeps per-chain, per-asset balances near a configured base. Rebalancing triggers when a balance falls to `(1 - triggerPercentage) × baseBalance`. Base balances are expressed in USD value (treated as $1 per stablecoin), keyed by asset symbol and then by numeric chain ID.

```toml lineNumbers
[rebalancing]
triggerPercentage = 0.5   # trigger when balance ≤ 50% of base

[rebalancing.baseBalances."USDC"]
"1"     = "10000"   # Ethereum: $10k USDC base
"8453"  = "10000"   # Base
"42161" = "10000"   # Arbitrum

[rebalancing.baseBalances."USDT"]
"1"     = "10000"
"8453"  = "10000"
"42161" = "10000"
```

### Allowlist

The optional `[allowlist]` section restricts which order `user` addresses the filler will process. Omit the section entirely to accept orders from all users (the default). When present, only listed users are accepted; address comparisons are case-insensitive.

```toml lineNumbers
[allowlist]
# Users eligible across all source chains
users = [
    "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
]

# Per-source-chain overrides, keyed by state-machine ID. Merged with the global list.
[allowlist.bySource]
"EVM-1"     = ["0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222"]   # Ethereum-only partner
"EVM-42161" = ["0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333"]   # Arbitrum-only partner
```

A source chain whose merged set (global `users` + its `bySource` override) is empty rejects every order from that chain.

### Gas Fee Bump

UserOperation gas prices are bumped above the base `gasPrice` by configurable percentages. Defaults are `8%` for the priority fee and `10%` for the max fee. Override under `[simplex.gasFeeBump]`:

```toml lineNumbers
[simplex.gasFeeBump]
maxPriorityFeePerGasBumpPercent = 8    # added to base gasPrice for the priority fee
maxFeePerGasBumpPercent         = 10   # added to base gasPrice for the max fee
```

### Confirmation Policy

<Callout type="info">
Confirmation policies are configured per strategy. Both the Stable strategy and HyperFX can use confirmation policies for cross-chain orders.
</Callout>

Before processing a cross-chain order, Simplex waits for enough block confirmations to guard against chain reorganizations. The number of confirmations scales with order value using a curve — small orders are processed quickly, large orders wait longer. Same-chain orders always proceed without additional confirmation delay.

#### Built-in Defaults

Simplex ships with default confirmation policies for common chains. These apply automatically when no user-configured policy exists for a chain. User-configured policies override the default for that chain.

| Chain | Chain ID | Min ($1,000) | Max ($100,000) | Block Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ethereum | 1 | 2 blocks (~24s) | 15 blocks (~3m) | ~12s |
| BNB Chain | 56 | 2 blocks (~6s) | 3 blocks (~9s) | ~3s |
| Polygon | 137 | 2 blocks (~4s) | 32 blocks (~1m) | ~2s |
| Base | 8453 | 2 blocks (~4s) | 90 blocks (~3m) | ~2s |
| Arbitrum | 42161 | 8 blocks (~2s) | 720 blocks (~3m) | ~0.25s |

Values between the min and max order amounts are linearly interpolated.

#### Custom Overrides

Confirmation policies are configured **per strategy** under `[strategies.confirmationPolicies."<chainId>"]`. Unlisted chains keep their defaults:

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "stable"
bpsCurve = [
    { amount = "100",    value = 100 },
    { amount = "100000", value = 10  },
]

[strategies.confirmationPolicies."1"]     # Ethereum Mainnet (~12s blocks)
points = [
    { amount = "1000",   value = 3  },   # $1k → 3 blocks (~36s)
    { amount = "50000",  value = 15 },   # $50k → 15 blocks (~3m)
    { amount = "100000", value = 20 },   # $100k → 20 blocks (~4m)
]

[strategies.confirmationPolicies."56"]    # BSC (~3s blocks)
points = [
    { amount = "1000",   value = 2  },
    { amount = "100000", value = 5  },
]
```

HyperFX uses the same schema:

```toml lineNumbers
[[strategies]]
type = "hyperfx"
maxOrderUsd = 5000

[strategies.token1]
"EVM-56"  = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnBsc"
"EVM-137" = "0xExoticTokenAddressOnPolygon"

[strategies.confirmationPolicies."56"]    # BSC
points = [
    { amount = "1",    value = 3  },
    { amount = "500",  value = 6  },
    { amount = "5000", value = 15 },
]

[strategies.confirmationPolicies."42161"] # Arbitrum
points = [
    { amount = "2",    value = 2  },
    { amount = "1000", value = 5  },
    { amount = "8000", value = 10 },
]
```

<Callout type="info">
Confirmation policies are optional — built-in defaults cover Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, and Unichain. Custom <code>[strategies.confirmationPolicies."&lt;chainId&gt;"]</code> entries override the default for that chain only.
</Callout>

### RPC Quorum

Each `[[chains]]` entry declares its RPC endpoints as a non-empty array in `rpcUrls`. Simplex validates the array at startup and rejects it if any two URLs share a hostname, so a "quorum" of aliases pointing at the same upstream is caught before the filler starts.

```toml lineNumbers
[[chains]]  # Ethereum
rpcUrls = [
    "https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY",
    "https://mainnet.infura.io/v3/YOUR_KEY",
    "https://rpc.ankr.com/eth/YOUR_KEY",
]
bundlerUrl = "https://..."
```

When two or more URLs are configured, the event monitor fans every `eth_getLogs` batch out to all providers in parallel and accepts the batch once a **Byzantine-fault-tolerant quorum** of providers agree. The threshold is the standard BFT bound — strictly more than two thirds, i.e. `floor(2N/3) + 1` providers:

| Providers (N) | Quorum threshold | Faults tolerated |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 | 0 |
| 4 | 3 | 1 |
| 5 | 4 | 1 |
| 7 | 5 | 2 |
| 10 | 7 | 3 |

Provider errors, timeouts, and divergent results are all tolerated up to the BFT bound. Beyond it, the batch fails with a `QuorumError` that enumerates each failing URL and the size of the largest agreeing group — the scan cursor does not advance, so the same range is retried on the next tick. Agreement is computed by sorting logs by `(blockNumber, logIndex, transactionHash)` and comparing only the consensus-relevant JSON-RPC fields (`address`, `blockHash`, `blockNumber`, `data`, `logIndex`, `removed`, `topics`, `transactionHash`, `transactionIndex`); provider-added extras such as `blockTimestamp` are deliberately excluded so debug metadata on one node does not manufacture a quorum failure. `getBlockNumber` resolves to the highest block at which `floor(2N/3) + 1` providers have indexed — preventing the scanner from running ahead of BFT-supported state.

A single-entry `rpcUrls` array is legal and keeps the pre-existing single-provider behaviour; the quorum machinery only engages when you list more than one endpoint. **To actually tolerate a faulty or co-opted provider you need at least four endpoints** — with three, the threshold is still three and any single failure halts scanning.

#### Why this matters for cross-chain orders

On a cross-chain fill, Simplex observes an `OrderPlaced` (or `PartialFill` / `OrderFilled`) event on the source chain and then commits capital on the destination chain. Unlike same-chain fills — where the destination `fillOrder` call will revert if the source-chain order does not exist — cross-chain bids submitted through Hyperbridge are evaluated from the filler's own reading of source-chain state. A single RPC is therefore both an availability and an integrity choke point: if it lies about which orders were placed, the filler can be induced to pay out against events that never happened, and there is no on-chain safety net to catch it after the fact.

<Callout type="warn">
Co-opted RPC nodes are not hypothetical. LayerZero has publicly disclosed an incident where an RPC endpoint serving part of their relaying path was compromised — see [LayerZero's post-mortem thread](https://x.com/LayerZero_Core/status/2046081551574983137?s=20). Quorum queries turn that failure mode from "one bad node silently succeeds" into "one bad node fails the batch and halts the scan".
</Callout>

The practical guidance is to configure **at least two organisationally independent providers** (e.g. Alchemy **and** Infura, not two Alchemy regions) for every chain that can act as a source of a cross-chain order. Three or more is better for chains with large notional flow — each additional independent provider raises the bar for an attacker from "compromise one vendor" to "compromise all of them simultaneously for the duration of the fill window". The cost is a slightly higher RPC bill and the tail latency of the slowest provider in each batch; the benefit is that event-driven bids are only acted on when every independent witness agrees on what the source chain actually emitted.

## Requirements

You need an EVM wallet (configured via `[simplex.signer]`) funded with native tokens for gas and stablecoins to fill orders with — minimum $10,000 equivalent per chain is a reasonable starting point. For HyperFX, also hold the exotic token on each chain, plus a Substrate account with BRIDGE tokens for Hyperbridge extrinsic fees. These extrinsic fees are claimable — Simplex claims them automatically after each batch of bids is executed on-chain or when the filler stops.

RPC endpoints must be from a premium provider (Alchemy Pro, Infura Growth+, QuickNode Pro). Archive node access is required for storage slot queries and gas simulation. Free-tier RPCs will not work reliably. For chains that can source cross-chain orders, configure at least two organisationally independent providers in `rpcUrls` so the event monitor runs in quorum mode — see [RPC Quorum](#rpc-quorum).

## Troubleshooting

For verbose output, set `logging = "debug"` in `[simplex]`. Report bugs to the Hyperbridge GitHub with full logs (redact private keys).

### **No profitable strategy found**
Gas prices may be too high relative to the order fee, or your `bpsCurve` thresholds are set too conservatively. Check balances on the destination chain and review current gas prices.

### **Insufficient token balances**
Deposit more stablecoins (and exotic tokens for HyperFX) on the destination chains.

### **RPC rate limiting (429 errors)**
Switch to a premium RPC provider or reduce `maxConcurrentOrders`.

### **HyperFX bid submission fails**
Confirm `substratePrivateKey`, `hyperbridgeWsUrl`, and `bundlerUrl` are set in `[simplex]`, and that your Substrate account has BRIDGE tokens. On chains with the Circle Paymaster, make sure the filler's smart account holds ≥1 USDC so the paymaster can cover gas. On chains without the paymaster (e.g. BSC), the filler needs native balance — Simplex automatically tops up the ERC-4337 EntryPoint deposit to cover `targetGasUnits` (default 3M) at current gas price. If using MPC Vault, verify the client-signer container is running and reachable.

### **Funding venue withdrawal failed**
Confirm the LP position has sufficient liquidity and that the token addresses match the exotic token configured in HyperFX. Verify the `tokenId` exists and is owned by the solver account. Check logs for specific revert reasons.

### **Venue price returns null / bid-ask not updating**
Confirm the configured positions contain a pool that pairs the exotic token with **USDC or USDT**. Pools with other quote tokens cannot derive a USD price from the Uniswap V4 venue. Check that the position's `tokenId` is valid and owned by the solver.

# HyperbridgeLzEndpoint

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/evm/lz-endpoint.mdx

title: LayerZero Endpoint Adapter
description: Drop-in LayerZero V2 endpoint backed by Hyperbridge's ISMP protocol for existing OFTs and OApps.

# HyperbridgeLzEndpoint

`HyperbridgeLzEndpoint` is a drop-in replacement for the LayerZero V2 endpoint that routes all cross-chain messages through Hyperbridge's ISMP protocol. Existing OFTs and OApps can point to this contract as their endpoint to use Hyperbridge for cross-chain transport without any code changes.

The contract implements `ILayerZeroEndpointV2` for full OApp/OFT compatibility and inherits [HyperApp](/developers/evm/api/hyperapp) for ISMP message handling.

## How It Works

When an OApp calls `send()` on the endpoint, the adapter encodes the LayerZero message into an ISMP POST request body and dispatches it through Hyperbridge. On the destination chain, the same adapter receives the ISMP message via `onAccept()`, decodes it back into LayerZero format, and delivers it to the destination OApp via `lzReceive()`.

    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect x="620" y="20" width="160" height="50" rx="8" fill="#1c1917" stroke="#78716c" strokeWidth="1"/>
  <text x="700" y="50" textAnchor="middle" fill="#d6d3d1" fontSize="13" fontFamily="monospace">OFT / OApp</text>

The adapter assumes the same contract address on all chains via CREATE2 deployment. It verifies incoming messages by checking that `request.from` matches its own address — if it's the same contract on both chains, only legitimate messages from the adapter on the source chain are accepted.

### Compose Support

The adapter supports LayerZero's two-step compose pattern. When an OApp calls `sendCompose()` during `lzReceive()`, the message hash is queued. A relayer or executor then calls `lzCompose()` with the full message, which is verified against the queued hash before being delivered to the target `ILayerZeroComposer`.

### Fee Model

Fees are paid in the host's fee token or native token, consistent with Hyperbridge's standard fee model. The adapter charges a per-destination relayer fee (configurable by the owner) on top of the protocol fee. The default relayer fee is $0.30, derived from the fee token's decimals.

## Deployment

<Steps>
<Step>
### Deploy with CREATE2

The adapter must have the same address on all chains so it can verify cross-chain message sources.

```solidity lineNumbers
import {HyperbridgeLzEndpoint} from "@hyperbridge/lz-endpoint/HyperbridgeLzEndpoint.sol";

bytes32 salt = keccak256("hyperbridge-lz-v1");
HyperbridgeLzEndpoint endpoint = new HyperbridgeLzEndpoint{salt: salt}(admin);
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Configure the host and local EID

```solidity lineNumbers
endpoint.setHost(ISMP_HOST_ADDRESS, LOCAL_LZ_EID);
```

This also sets the default relayer fee to $0.30 based on the host's fee token decimals.
</Step>
<Step>
### Register EID mappings

Map each LayerZero endpoint ID to its corresponding ISMP state machine identifier:

```solidity lineNumbers
import {StateMachine} from "@hyperbridge/core/libraries/StateMachine.sol";

// Ethereum = LZ EID 30001, ISMP EVM-1
endpoint.setEidMapping(30001, StateMachine.evm(1));

// Arbitrum = LZ EID 30110, ISMP EVM-42161
endpoint.setEidMapping(30110, StateMachine.evm(42161));

// Base = LZ EID 30184, ISMP EVM-8453
endpoint.setEidMapping(30184, StateMachine.evm(8453));
```
</Step>
</Steps>

## Using with an OFT

### New Deployments

Pass the `HyperbridgeLzEndpoint` address as the endpoint in the OFT constructor:

```solidity lineNumbers
import {OFT} from "@layerzerolabs/oft-evm/contracts/OFT.sol";

OFT oft = new OFT(
    "My Token",
    "MTK",
    address(hyperbridgeLzEndpoint), // use adapter instead of LZ endpoint
    msg.sender
);
```

Then configure peers as usual via `setPeer(dstEid, peerAddress)`. The adapter handles routing transparently — the OFT doesn't need to know about ISMP.

### Migrating Existing Proxy Deployments

For OFTs deployed behind an upgradeable proxy (e.g. UUPS or TransparentProxy), you can migrate to Hyperbridge by upgrading the implementation to one that points to the `HyperbridgeLzEndpoint`. The storage layout is unchanged — the only difference in the new implementation is the endpoint address passed to the constructor, which is stored as an immutable and lives in bytecode, not storage:

<Steps>
<Step>
### Deploy a new implementation

Deploy a new OFT implementation that uses the `HyperbridgeLzEndpoint` as its endpoint:

```solidity lineNumbers
OFTUpgradeable newImpl = new OFTUpgradeable(address(hyperbridgeLzEndpoint));
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Upgrade the proxy

Upgrade the proxy to the new implementation. For UUPS proxies:

```solidity lineNumbers
proxy.upgradeToAndCall(address(newImpl), "");
```

For TransparentProxy:

```solidity lineNumbers
ProxyAdmin(proxyAdmin).upgradeAndCall(proxy, address(newImpl), "");
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Update peers

Re-configure peers to point to the `HyperbridgeLzEndpoint` deployments on each chain:

```solidity lineNumbers
OFT(proxy).setPeer(dstEid, peerAddress);
```
</Step>
</Steps>

## Using with an OApp

The same approach works for any OApp, not just OFTs.

### New Deployments

Pass the `HyperbridgeLzEndpoint` as the endpoint in the OApp constructor:

```solidity lineNumbers
import {OApp} from "@layerzerolabs/oapp-evm/contracts/oapp/OApp.sol";

contract MyOApp is OApp {
    constructor(address endpoint, address owner) OApp(endpoint, owner) {}

    // your cross-chain logic
}

MyOApp app = new MyOApp(address(hyperbridgeLzEndpoint), msg.sender);
```

All `_lzSend()` calls from your OApp will route through Hyperbridge automatically. Incoming messages arrive via `_lzReceive()` as usual.

### Migrating Existing Proxy Deployments

Same as OFTs — the endpoint is an immutable in bytecode, so deploy a new implementation with the adapter address and upgrade the proxy. Storage layout is unchanged.

# GET Requests

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/evm/messaging/get-requests.mdx

title: GET Requests
description: Learn how to dispatch GET requests to perform asynchronous reads of remote blockchain state via Hyperbridge.

# GET Requests

GET requests allow contracts to perform asynchronous reads of a counterparty blockchain's state. This powerful feature enables you to read data from any chain without needing to trust oracles or intermediaries - all state reads are cryptographically verified by Hyperbridge.

## Important Considerations

**GET requests are read-only operations** - they cannot modify state on the destination chain. GET requests read storage directly from the blockchain's state trie and return the values through a cryptographic proof. The response is delivered via the `onGetResponse` callback in your contract.

## The `DispatchGet` Struct

A GET request is created using the `DispatchGet` struct:

```solidity lineNumbers
// An object for dispatching get requests 
struct DispatchGet {
    // bytes representation of the destination state machine
    bytes dest;
    // height at which to read the state machine
    uint64 height;
    // Storage keys to read
    bytes[] keys;
    // timeout for this request in seconds
    uint64 timeout;
    // Optional relayer fee for delivering the response back to the source chain
    uint256 fee;
    // Application-specific metadata
    bytes context;
}
```

## Dispatch Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `dest` | Destination chain whose state should be read (e.g., `StateMachine.evm(1)` for Ethereum Mainnet). |
| `height` | Block height at which to read the state. Only heights available on hyperbridge can be used.  |
| `keys` | Array of storage keys to read. See the Storage Keys section for how to construct keys for different chain types. |
| `timeout` | Time in seconds for message validity eg 3600 for a timeout of 1 hour, or 0 for no timeout. If the timeout is set to a non-zero value, requests that have exceeded this timeout will be rejected. |
| `fee` | Optional relayer fee for delivering the response back to the source chain. Set to zero if self-relaying the `GetResponse`. |
| `context` | Application-specific metadata that will be available in the `onGetResponse` callback. Use this to track which request is which. |

## Dispatching a GET Request

Here's a complete example of how to dispatch a GET request:

```solidity lineNumbers
function readRemoteBalance(
    address token,
    address account,
    bytes memory dest
) public payable returns (bytes32) {
    // Calculate the storage slot for balanceOf[account]
    bytes32 slot = keccak256(abi.encode(account, uint256(0))); // Assuming balances at slot 0

    // Construct the storage key (20 bytes address + 32 bytes slot)
    bytes[] memory keys = new bytes[](1);
    keys[0] = bytes.concat(bytes20(token), slot);

    // Encode context to track this request
    bytes memory context = abi.encode(token, account);

    DispatchGet memory request = DispatchGet({
        dest: dest,
        height: 0, // Latest finalized block
        keys: keys,
        timeout: 3600, // 1 hour
        fee: msg.value,
        context: new bytes(0) // empty for this use-case
    });

    return IDispatcher(_host).dispatch{value: msg.value}(request);
}
```

### Code Breakdown

1. **Calculate storage slot** - Determine the exact storage location you want to read
2. **Construct storage keys** - Format keys according to the chain type (20 or 52 bytes for EVM)
3. **Add context** - Encode any metadata you'll need in the callback
4. **Create DispatchGet struct** - Populate all required fields
5. **Dispatch the request** - Call `IDispatcher(_host).dispatch()` with the GET request and protocol fee
6. **Return commitment hash** - The function returns a unique identifier for tracking the request

## Storage Keys

The `keys` parameter is an array of raw storage keys that will be used to fetch values from the counterparty chain. The method for deriving these keys depends on the type of chain you're querying.

### EVM Storage Keys

For EVM chains, storage keys must be either **20 bytes** or **52 bytes**:

#### Contract Storage Slots

Concatenation of contract address (20 bytes) + storage slot hash (32 bytes)

- Use this to read specific storage slots in a contract
- The slot hash is computed using Solidity's storage layout rules
- Format: `bytes.concat(bytes20(contractAddress), bytes32(storageSlot))`

**Example:**

```solidity lineNumbers
// Reading balances[account] from an ERC20 at slot 0
address token = 0x1234...;
address account = 0x5678...;
bytes32 slot = keccak256(abi.encode(account, uint256(0)));
bytes memory key = bytes.concat(bytes20(token), slot);
```

#### Account State

Single contract address (20 bytes)

- Use this to read account-level information
- Returns account nonce, balance, code hash, and storage root
- Format: `bytes20(accountAddress)`

**Example:**

```solidity lineNumbers
// Reading account state for an address
address account = 0x1234...;
bytes memory key = bytes20(account);
```

### Substrate Storage Keys

For Substrate/Polkadot chains, storage keys depend on the storage type:

#### StorageValue

<Tabs items={['Substrate', 'Solidity']}>
<Tab value="Substrate">

```rust lineNumbers
// In Substrate pallet
#[pallet::storage]
pub type MyValue<T> = StorageValue<_, u128>;
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Solidity">

```solidity lineNumbers
// Hash the pallet name and storage item name
bytes memory key = bytes.concat(
    xxhash128("MyPallet"),
    xxhash128("MyValue")
);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

#### StorageMap

<Tabs items={['Substrate', 'Solidity']}>
<Tab value="Substrate">

```rust lineNumbers
// In Substrate pallet
#[pallet::storage]
pub type Balances<T> = StorageMap<_, Blake2_128Concat, AccountId, Balance>;
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Solidity">

```solidity lineNumbers
// Key construction
bytes memory key = bytes.concat(
    xxhash128("MyPallet"),
    xxhash128("Balances"),
    blake2_128(accountId),
    accountId
);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

#### StorageDoubleMap and StorageNMap

For more complex storage types, consult the [Substrate storage documentation](https://docs.substrate.io/build/runtime-storage/).

<Callout type="warning" title="GET Response Values are Encoded">
All values returned in GET responses are either **RLP-encoded** or **SCALE-encoded** because they come directly from the state trie. You must use the appropriate decoding library (like `solidity-rlp` for RLP or `scale-codec` for SCALE) to decode the values before using them. Do not use `abi.decode()` on GET response values.
</Callout>

## Practical Examples
<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Examples Requests">

<Tabs items={['Reading ERC20 Balance', 'Reading Uniswap V2 Reserves', 'Reading Multiple Slots']}>
<Tab value="Reading ERC20 Balance">

```solidity lineNumbers title="RemoteBalanceChecker.sol"
contract RemoteBalanceChecker is HyperApp {
    address private _host;
    
    constructor(address host) {
        _host = host;
    }
    
    function host() public override view returns (address) {
        return _host;
    }

    function checkRemoteBalance(
        address token,
        address account,
        bytes memory destChain,
        uint256 height
    ) public payable returns (bytes32) {
        // Calculate storage slot for balances[account]
        // Assuming balances is at slot 0
        bytes32 slot = keccak256(abi.encode(account, uint256(0)));
        
        // Construct 52-byte storage key
        bytes[] memory keys = new bytes[](1);
        keys[0] = bytes.concat(bytes20(token), slot);
        
        // Use context to remember who initiated this request
        bytes memory context = abi.encode(msg.sender, token, account);
        
        DispatchGet memory request = DispatchGet({
            dest: destChain,
            height: height,
            keys: keys,
            timeout: 0,
            fee: msg.value,
            context: context
        });
        
        bytes32 commitment = IDispatcher(_host).dispatch{value: msg.value}(request);
        
        return commitment;
    }
    
    // Receive the response
    function onGetResponse(GetResponse memory response) 
        external 
        override 
        onlyHost 
    {
        // Decode context
        (address initiator, address token, address account) = abi.decode(
            response.context,
            (address, address, address)
        );
        
        // response.values[0] could be empty if the user has no balance
        if (response.values.length == 0) {
            emit BalanceRetrieved(initiator, token, account, 0);
            return;
        }
        
        // Decode balance from response (values are RLP-encoded from state trie)
        uint256 balance = RLPReader.toUint(response.values[0]);
        
        // Process the balance
        emit BalanceRetrieved(initiator, token, account, balance);
    }
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Reading Uniswap V2 Reserves">

```solidity lineNumbers title="UniswapPriceOracle.sol" icon="solidity"
contract UniswapPriceOracle is HyperApp {
    function fetchPairReserves(address pair, bytes memory destChain, uint256 height) 
        public 
        payable 
        returns (bytes32) 
    {
        // Uniswap V2 stores reserves at slot 8
        bytes32 reservesSlot = bytes32(uint256(8));
        
        bytes[] memory keys = new bytes[](1);
        keys[0] = bytes.concat(bytes20(pair), reservesSlot);
        
        DispatchGet memory request = DispatchGet({
            dest: destChain,
            height: height,
            keys: keys,
            timeout: 0, // 30 minutes
            fee: msg.value,
            context: abi.encode(pair)
        });
        
        return IDispatcher(_host).dispatch{value: msg.value}(request);
    }
    
    function onGetResponse(GetResponse memory response) 
        external 
        override 
        onlyHost 
    {
        address pair = abi.decode(response.context, (address));
        
        // Decode reserves from RLP-encoded storage value
        // The value is a packed uint256 with reserve0, reserve1, and timestamp
        uint256 packedValue = RLPReader.toUint(response.values[0]);
        
        // Extract packed values (reserve0, reserve1, blockTimestampLast)
        uint112 reserve0 = uint112(packedValue);
        uint112 reserve1 = uint112(packedValue >> 112);
        uint32 blockTimestampLast = uint32(packedValue >> 224);
        
        // Calculate price and emit event
        uint256 price = (uint256(reserve1) * 1e18) / uint256(reserve0);
        emit PriceUpdated(pair, price, reserve0, reserve1, blockTimestampLast);
    }
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Reading Multiple Slots">

```solidity lineNumbers title="MultipleSlotReader.sol" icon="solidity"
function readMultipleSlots(
    address contract_,
    bytes32[] memory slots,
    uint256 height,
    bytes memory dest
) public payable returns (bytes32) {
    // Construct keys for multiple slots
    bytes[] memory keys = new bytes[](slots.length);
    for (uint256 i = 0; i < slots.length; i++) {
        keys[i] = bytes.concat(bytes20(contract_), slots[i]);
    }
    
    DispatchGet memory getRequest = DispatchGet({
        dest: dest,
        height: height,
        keys: keys,
        timeout: 0,
        fee: msg.value,
        context: abi.encode(contract_, slots)
    });
    
    return IDispatcher(_host).dispatch{value: msg.value}(getRequest);
}
```

</Tab>
