# EvmChain

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain.mdx

title: EvmChain
description: API reference for EvmChain - interact with EVM-compatible chains in the Hyperbridge protocol.

# EvmChain

The `EvmChain` class provides methods for interacting with EVM-compatible chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, etc.) in the Hyperbridge protocol. It handles proof generation, state queries, and cross-chain message verification.

```typescript lineNumbers
class EvmChain implements IChain
```

## Static Methods

### EvmChain.create(rpcUrl, bundlerUrl?)

Auto-detects the chain ID from the RPC endpoint and resolves the correct `IsmpHost` contract address for that chain. This is the recommended way to instantiate `EvmChain` for known Hyperbridge deployments.

```typescript lineNumbers
static async create(rpcUrl: string, bundlerUrl?: string): Promise<EvmChain>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `rpcUrl` | `string` | HTTP(S) RPC URL of the EVM node |
| `bundlerUrl` | `string` | Optional. ERC-4337 bundler URL for account abstraction support |

**Returns:** `Promise<EvmChain>` — A fully initialized `EvmChain` instance

**Throws:** If the chain ID returned by the RPC is not a known Hyperbridge deployment

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { EvmChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// Auto-detect chain from RPC
const chain = await EvmChain.create("https://mainnet.base.org")

// With ERC-4337 bundler for IntentGateway
const destChain = await EvmChain.create(
  "https://arb-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY",
  "https://bundler.example.com"
)
```

### EvmChain.fromParams(params)

Creates an `EvmChain` instance from a fully-specified params object. Use this when you already know the chain ID and `IsmpHost` address and don't need auto-detection.

```typescript lineNumbers
static fromParams(params: EvmChainParams): EvmChain
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `params.chainId` | `number` | The EVM chain ID (e.g., 1 for Ethereum, 42161 for Arbitrum) |
| `params.rpcUrl` | `string` | RPC URL for the chain (must be an archive node for proof queries) |
| `params.host` | `HexString` | Address of the IsmpHost contract on this chain |
| `params.consensusStateId` | `string` | Optional. Consensus state identifier on Hyperbridge (auto-detected for known chains) |
| `params.bundlerUrl` | `string` | Optional. ERC-4337 bundler URL for account abstraction support |

**Returns:** `EvmChain`

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { EvmChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const ethereumChain = EvmChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 1,
  rpcUrl: "https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY",
  host: "0x87ea459...",
  consensusStateId: "ETH0" // Optional, auto-detected for known chains
})

const arbitrumChain = EvmChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 42161,
  rpcUrl: "https://arb-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY",
  host: "0x42fa123...",
  bundlerUrl: "https://bundler.example.com" // Optional, for ERC-4337 support
})
```

## Supported Chains

The `EvmChain` class supports all EVM-compatible chains. Pre-configured defaults include:

| Chain | Chain ID | Default Consensus State ID |
|-------|----------|---------------------------|
| Ethereum Mainnet | 1 | ETH0 |
| Ethereum Sepolia | 11155111 | ETH0 |
| Arbitrum One | 42161 | ETH0 |
| Arbitrum Sepolia | 421614 | ETH0 |
| Optimism | 10 | ETH0 |
| Optimism Sepolia | 11155420 | ETH0 |
| Base | 8453 | ETH0 |
| Base Sepolia | 84532 | ETH0 |
| Unichain | 130 | ETH0 |
| Soneium | 1868 | ETH0 |
| Polygon | 137 | POLY |
| Polygon Amoy | 80002 | POLY |
| BSC | 56 | BSC0 |
| BSC Testnet | 97 | BSC0 |
| Gnosis | 100 | GNO0 |
| Gnosis Chiado | 10200 | GNO0 |
| Polkadot Asset Hub (Paseo) | 420420417 | PAS0 |

## Important Notes

### Archive Node Requirement

**Critical:** The RPC URL must point to an archive node. Regular nodes only retain recent state and cannot provide storage proofs for older blocks, which are essential for:
- Timeout proof generation
- Historical state verification
- Cross-chain message validation

### Consensus State IDs

Consensus state IDs identify how a chain is verified on Hyperbridge:
- Chains using Ethereum consensus share `ETH0`
- Polygon uses `POLY`
- BSC uses `BSC0`
- Gnosis uses `GNO0`

For custom chains, specify the appropriate `consensusStateId` based on how the chain is configured on Hyperbridge.

# HyperFungibleToken

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/hyper-fungible-token.mdx

title: HyperFungibleToken
description: API reference for the HyperFungibleToken SDK class — cross-chain token bridging with fee quoting, ERC165 detection, and ISMP status tracking.

# HyperFungibleToken

The `HyperFungibleToken` class provides a generator-based flow for bridging tokens cross-chain via Hyperbridge. It supports both `HyperFungibleToken` (burn/mint) and `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` (lock/unlock) contracts, with automatic type detection via ERC165.

Unlike the deprecated [TokenGateway](/developers/sdk/api/token-gateway), each HyperFungibleToken is its own bridge application — no governance overhead or shared custody pool.

## Constructor

### new HyperFungibleToken(params)

```typescript lineNumbers
new HyperFungibleToken(params: {
  source: EvmChain
  dest: EvmChain
  client?: IsmpClient
})
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `params.source` | `EvmChain` | Source EVM chain where tokens are sent from |
| `params.dest` | `EvmChain` | Destination EVM chain where tokens are received |
| `params.client` | `IsmpClient` | Optional ISMP client for tracking request status after submission. If not provided, the bridge generator terminates at the `submitted` step. |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import {
  HyperFungibleToken,
  IsmpClient,
  createQueryClient,
  EvmChain,
  SubstrateChain,
} from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// EvmChain.create auto-detects chain ID and resolves the IsmpHost address
const source = await EvmChain.create("https://data-seed-prebsc-1-s1.binance.org:8545")
const dest = await EvmChain.create("https://rpc-amoy.polygon.technology")

/* Without IsmpClient — generator ends at "submitted" */
const hft = new HyperFungibleToken({ source, dest })

/* With IsmpClient — generator streams status updates */
const hyperbridge = await SubstrateChain.connect({
  wsUrl: "wss://gargantua.rpc.polytope.technology",
  consensusStateId: "PAS0",
  hasher: "Keccak",
  stateMachineId: "KUSAMA-4009",
})

const queryClient = createQueryClient({
  url: "https://gargantua.indexer.polytope.technology",
})

const ismpClient = new IsmpClient({
  queryClient,
  source,
  dest,
  hyperbridge,
  pollInterval: 5_000,
})

const hftWithTracking = new HyperFungibleToken({ source, dest, client: ismpClient })
```

## Methods

### isWrapped(tokenAddress)

Detects whether a token contract is a `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` via ERC165 interface detection.

```typescript lineNumbers
async isWrapped(tokenAddress: Address): Promise<boolean>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `tokenAddress` | `Address` | The token contract address to check |

**Returns:** `true` if the contract implements `IWrappedHyperFungibleToken` (interface ID `0xe23d9765`), `false` otherwise.

### quote(params)

Quotes the fee for a cross-chain send. The fee estimation pipeline:

1. Estimates gas for delivering the message on the destination chain
2. Converts the dest gas cost to the dest chain's fee token via Uniswap
3. Scales decimals if source and dest fee tokens differ in precision
4. Calls the on-chain `quote()` and `quote()` methods on the token contract

```typescript lineNumbers
async quote(params: BridgeParams): Promise<QuoteResult>
```

**Parameters:** See [BridgeParams](#bridgeparams).

**Returns:** `Promise<QuoteResult>`

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `totalNativeCost` | `bigint` | Native token amount needed as `msg.value` for `send()` (protocol fee + relayer fee). May be `0n` if no Uniswap router is available on the source chain. |
| `totalFeeTokenCost` | `bigint` | Total fee in the host's fee token (protocol fee + relayer fee) |
| `relayerFeeInFeeToken` | `bigint` | Relayer fee component in the source chain's fee token |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const fee = await hft.quote({
  token: "0x...",
  from: senderAddress,
  to: recipientAddress,
  amount: parseEther("100"),
  dest: "EVM-80002",
})

console.log(`Native cost: ${fee.totalNativeCost}`)
console.log(`Fee token cost: ${fee.totalFeeTokenCost}`)
console.log(`Relayer fee: ${fee.relayerFeeInFeeToken}`)
```

### bridge(params)

Async generator that yields steps the caller must execute to complete a cross-chain token transfer. The generator handles ERC20 approvals, fee quoting, transaction building, commitment extraction, and ISMP status streaming.

```typescript lineNumbers
async *bridge(params: BridgeParams): AsyncGenerator<BridgeStep, void, HexString | undefined>
```

**Parameters:** See [BridgeParams](#bridgeparams).

**Yields:** See [BridgeStep](#bridgestep).

The generator flow:

<Steps>
<Step>
#### Approve (conditional)

For `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` with a non-WETH underlying token: yields an `approve` step if the current allowance is less than the transfer amount.

When `payInFeeToken` is `true`: yields an `approve` step for the fee token if the current allowance is insufficient.
</Step>
<Step>
#### Send

Yields a `send` step with the encoded `send()` calldata and the appropriate `value` (native fee or `0n` if paying in fee token). **The caller must resume the generator with the submitted transaction hash.**
</Step>
<Step>
#### Submitted

After the send transaction is mined, extracts the ISMP commitment from the `Sent` event logs and yields a `submitted` step.
</Step>
<Step>
#### Status (requires IsmpClient)

If an `IsmpClient` was provided, streams ISMP request status updates until a terminal state is reached.
</Step>
</Steps>

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http } from "viem"
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts"
import { bscTestnet } from "viem/chains"

const account = privateKeyToAccount(PRIVATE_KEY)
const walletClient = createWalletClient({
  account,
  chain: bscTestnet,
  transport: http(BSC_RPC),
})
const publicClient = createPublicClient({
  chain: bscTestnet,
  transport: http(BSC_RPC),
})

const gen = hft.bridge({
  token: "0x...",
  from: account.address,
  to: recipientAddress,
  amount: parseEther("1"),
  dest: "EVM-80002",
  timeout: 3600n,
  payInFeeToken: true,
})

let result = await gen.next()

while (!result.done) {
  const step = result.value
  if (!step) break

  if (step.type === "approve") {
    const hash = await walletClient.sendTransaction({
      to: step.tx.to,
      data: step.tx.data,
    })
    await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })
    result = await gen.next()
    continue
  }

  if (step.type === "send") {
    const hash = await walletClient.sendTransaction({
      to: step.tx.to,
      data: step.tx.data,
      value: step.tx.value,
    })
    /* Resume with the tx hash */
    result = await gen.next(hash)
    continue
  }

  if (step.type === "submitted") {
    console.log("Commitment:", step.commitment)
    result = await gen.next()
    continue
  }

  if (step.type === "status") {
    console.log(`Status: ${step.status}`)
    if (step.status === "DESTINATION" || step.status === "TIMED_OUT") break
    result = await gen.next()
    continue
  }

  result = await gen.next()
}
```

## Types

### BridgeParams

```typescript lineNumbers
interface BridgeParams {
  /** Address of the HFT or WrappedHFT contract on the source chain */
  token: Address
  /** The sender's address (needed for allowance checks and fee quoting) */
  from: Address
  /** Recipient on the destination chain (20 bytes for EVM, 32 bytes for substrate) */
  to: HexString | Uint8Array
  /** Amount of tokens to send (in token decimals) */
  amount: bigint
  /** Destination state machine ID (e.g. "EVM-97") */
  dest: string | Uint8Array
  /** Request timeout in seconds (default: 3600) */
  timeout?: bigint
  /** Optional calldata to execute on the destination chain */
  data?: HexString
  /** Pay fees in the host's feeToken instead of native. Default: false */
  payInFeeToken?: boolean
  /** Relayer fee override in feeToken units. If not set, automatically
      estimated from destination gas cost. Set to 0n for self-relay. */
  relayerFee?: bigint
}
```

### BridgeStep

```typescript lineNumbers
type BridgeStep =
  | { type: "approve"; tx: { to: Address; data: HexString } }
  | { type: "send"; tx: { to: Address; data: HexString; value: bigint } }
  | { type: "submitted"; commitment: HexString }
  | { type: "status" } & RequestStatusWithMetadata
```

| Step | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `approve` | ERC20 approval transaction. Yielded for WrappedHFT underlying tokens or fee token approvals. |
| `send` | The cross-chain send transaction. Resume the generator with the tx hash. |
| `submitted` | Emitted after the send tx is mined. Contains the ISMP commitment hash. |
| `status` | ISMP request lifecycle update with full metadata. Only yielded if `client` was provided. |

**Status progression:**

```
SOURCE_FINALIZED → HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED → HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED → DESTINATION
```

The `HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED` status includes a `calldata` field in its metadata — the encoded proof that can be submitted to the destination chain's handler for self-relay.

### QuoteResult

```typescript lineNumbers
interface QuoteResult {
  /** Native token amount needed as msg.value for send() */
  totalNativeCost: bigint
  /** Total fee in the host's fee token */
  totalFeeTokenCost: bigint
  /** Relayer fee component in the source chain's fee token */
  relayerFeeInFeeToken: bigint
}
```

# IntentGateway

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/intent-gateway.mdx

title: IntentGateway
description: API reference for IntentGateway - place, execute, and cancel cross-chain intent orders via the Hyperbridge protocol.

# IntentGateway

The `IntentGateway` class is the high-level facade for the IntentGatewayV2 protocol. It orchestrates the full lifecycle of an intent-based cross-chain swap: order placement, bid collection, execution, cancellation, and status checks.

```typescript lineNumbers
class IntentGateway
```

## Static Methods

### IntentGateway.create(source, dest, intentsCoprocessor?)

Creates a fully initialised `IntentGateway` instance. Fetches fee tokens for both chains and optionally caches solver account bytecode before returning.

```typescript lineNumbers
static async create(
  source: IEvmChain,
  dest: IEvmChain,
  intentsCoprocessor?: IntentsCoprocessor,
): Promise<IntentGateway>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `source` | `IEvmChain` | Source chain where orders are placed and inputs are escrowed |
| `dest` | `IEvmChain` | Destination chain where solvers fill orders and deliver outputs |
| `intentsCoprocessor` | `IntentsCoprocessor` | Optional. Hyperbridge coprocessor client for bid fetching and UserOp submission |

**Returns:** `Promise<IntentGateway>`

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { EvmChain, IntentsCoprocessor, IntentGateway } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const source = await EvmChain.create("https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY")
const dest = await EvmChain.create(
  "https://arb-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY",
  "https://bundler.example.com",
)
const coprocessor = await IntentsCoprocessor.connect("wss://coprocessor.hyperbridge.network")

const gateway = await IntentGateway.create(source, dest, coprocessor)
```

## Properties

### source

The EVM chain on which orders are placed and inputs are escrowed.

**Type:** `IEvmChain`

### dest

The EVM chain on which solvers fill orders and deliver outputs.

**Type:** `IEvmChain`

### intentsCoprocessor

The Hyperbridge coprocessor client used for bid fetching and UserOp submission.

**Type:** `IntentsCoprocessor | undefined`

## Methods

### execute(order, graffiti?, options)

Consumer-driven bidirectional async generator that orchestrates the full order lifecycle: placement, fee estimation, and a timed bid auction. The caller signs the placement transaction when prompted, then **selects and executes a bid itself** — on `BIDS_RECEIVED` the generator yields executable [`Bid`](#bid) objects, and the caller feeds the [`SelectBidResult`](#selectbidresult) from `bid.execute()` back via `gen.next(result)`.

For the batteries-included "pick the best and go" behaviour, use [`executeBest`](#executebestorder-graffiti-options) instead.

```typescript lineNumbers
async *execute(
  order: Order,
  graffiti: HexString = DEFAULT_GRAFFITI,
  options: {
    auctionTimeMs: number
    maxPriorityFeePerGasBumpPercent?: number
    maxFeePerGasBumpPercent?: number
    pollIntervalMs?: number
    solver?: { address: HexString; timeoutMs: number }
  },
): AsyncGenerator<IntentOrderStatusUpdate, void, HexString | SelectBidResult | undefined>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `order` | `Order` | — | The order to place and execute. `order.fees` may be `0`; it is estimated automatically if so. |
| `graffiti` | `HexString` | `0x000...0` | Optional bytes32 tag for orderflow attribution/revenue share |
| `options.auctionTimeMs` | `number` | — | **Required.** Duration in ms to collect bids before surfacing them for selection |
| `options.maxPriorityFeePerGasBumpPercent` | `number` | `8` | Bump percentage applied to priority fee estimate |
| `options.maxFeePerGasBumpPercent` | `number` | `10` | Bump percentage applied to max fee estimate |
| `options.pollIntervalMs` | `number` | — | Interval between bid-polling attempts |
| `options.solver` | `{ address, timeoutMs }` | — | Restrict bids to `address` until `timeoutMs` elapses, then accept any solver |

**Yields:** `IntentOrderStatusUpdate`

**Receives (via `gen.next(value)`):** the signed placement tx (hash or raw tx) after `AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER`, and a `SelectBidResult` after `BIDS_RECEIVED` (or `undefined` to keep polling for fresh bids).

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const signer = createWalletClient({ ... })

// execute is a bidirectional generator — hold a reference to pass values back
const gen = gateway.execute(order, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI, { auctionTimeMs: 15_000 })

let input: HexString | SelectBidResult | undefined
while (true) {
  const { value: update, done } = await gen.next(input)
  input = undefined
  if (done) break

  switch (update.status) {
    case "AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER": {
      // Sign and broadcast the placement transaction, then feed the hash back.
      input = await signer.sendTransaction({
        to: update.to,
        data: update.data,
        value: update.value,
      })
      break
    }
    case "BIDS_RECEIVED": {
      // You own selection. Rank the bids however you like, simulate, execute.
      const sorted = await gateway.sortBids(order, update.bids)
      for (const bid of sorted) {
        try {
          await bid.simulate()
          input = await bid.execute() // feed the SelectBidResult back to the generator
          break
        } catch {
          // bid failed simulation/execution — try the next one
        }
      }
      // leaving `input` undefined keeps the auction polling for fresh bids
      break
    }
    case "BID_SELECTED":
      console.log("Solver selected:", update.selectedSolver)
      break
    case "FILLED":
      console.log("Order filled!")
      break
  }
}
```

### quoteIntent(params)

Quotes an intent using the SDK's intent quote strategies. The only supported strategy today is `uniswap_v4`, which always prices against the configured Base (`EVM-8453`) pool rather than the gateway destination chain. The method is strategy-shaped so future quote sources can be added without changing partner integrations.

Use `amountIn` and `amountOut` when constructing the `inputs` and `output.assets` for an IntentGateway V2 order.

```typescript lineNumbers
const gateway = await IntentGateway.create(source, dest)

const quote = await gateway.quoteIntent({
  tokenIn: {
    address: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    decimals: 6,
    symbol: "USDC",
  },
  tokenOut: {
    address: "0x46C85152bFe9f96829aA94755D9f915F9B10EF5F",
    decimals: 6,
    symbol: "cNGN",
  },
  amountIn: 100_000_000n,
})

console.log(quote.amountIn, quote.amountOut)
```

For pools not configured by the SDK, pass an explicit Uniswap V4 PoolKey:

```typescript lineNumbers
const quote = await gateway.quoteIntent({
  tokenIn,
  tokenOut,
  amountOut: 50_000_000n,
  uniswapV4: {
    poolKey: {
      currency0: "0x...",
      currency1: "0x...",
      fee: 1500,
      tickSpacing: 30,
      hooks: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
      quoterAddress: "0x0d5e0f971ed27fbff6c2837bf31316121532048d",
    },
  },
})
```

When passing an explicit PoolKey for cross-chain quotes, also pass `currencyIn` inside the `poolKey` override — the Base-side address of the input currency. It defaults to `tokenIn.address`, which only works when that address is part of the Base pool, and must equal `currency0` or `currency1`.

The result includes `amountIn`, `amountOut`, and quote metadata with the quote chain, V4 PoolKey, quoter address, and the IntentGateway protocol fee on the source chain (`protocolFeeBps`).

`amountIn` and `amountOut` already account for the IntentGateway protocol fee that the gateway deducts from order inputs. Exact-input quotes price the swap against the post-fee input, so `amountOut` is what you can expect after the fee; exact-output quotes return the gross `amountIn` you must supply so that, after the fee, enough remains to produce the requested `amountOut`. Use these amounts directly as the order's `inputs` and `output.assets` — no further fee adjustment is required. Apply only your own slippage tolerance:

```typescript lineNumbers
// `amountOut` already nets the gateway fee; add your slippage tolerance.
const minAmountOut = (quote.amountOut * (10_000n - SLIPPAGE_BPS)) / 10_000n
```

### executeBest(order, graffiti?, options)

Batteries-included variant of [`execute`](#executeorder-graffiti-options): places the order, then auto-selects and executes the best bid each round (sort → simulate → sign → submit) with no bid-selection input from the caller. The caller still signs the placement transaction (`AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER`); every other stage is handled automatically and surfaced for observation. If a round's bids all fail, it keeps polling for fresh bids until the deadline.

```typescript lineNumbers
async *executeBest(
  order: Order,
  graffiti: HexString = DEFAULT_GRAFFITI,
  options: {
    auctionTimeMs: number
    maxPriorityFeePerGasBumpPercent?: number
    maxFeePerGasBumpPercent?: number
    pollIntervalMs?: number
    solver?: { address: HexString; timeoutMs: number }
  },
): AsyncGenerator<IntentOrderStatusUpdate, void, HexString>
```

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const gen = gateway.executeBest(order, DEFAULT_GRAFFITI, { auctionTimeMs: 15_000 })
for await (const update of gen) {
  if (update.status === "AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER") {
    const txHash = await signer.sendTransaction({ to: update.to, data: update.data, value: update.value })
    await gen.next(txHash) // only the placement step needs feedback
  } else if (update.status === "FILLED") {
    console.log("Order filled!")
  }
}
```

### resume(order, options) / resumeBest(order, options)

Resume execution of a previously placed order (after an app restart or crash). The order must already be on-chain — it must have a valid `id` and `session`. There is no placement step, so a plain `for await` loop is sufficient.

- `resume` is consumer-driven, mirroring [`execute`](#executeorder-graffiti-options) (you select bids and feed back `SelectBidResult`).
- `resumeBest` is the autopilot, mirroring [`executeBest`](#executebestorder-graffiti-options).

```typescript lineNumbers
async *resume(order: Order, options: ResumeIntentOrderOptions):
  AsyncGenerator<IntentOrderStatusUpdate, void, SelectBidResult | undefined>

async *resumeBest(order: Order, options: ResumeIntentOrderOptions):
  AsyncGenerator<IntentOrderStatusUpdate, void>
```

`ResumeIntentOrderOptions` is `{ sessionPrivateKey?, auctionTimeMs, pollIntervalMs?, solver? }`.

### buildBids(order, bids, sessionPrivateKey?)

Decodes raw filler bids (as fetched from the coprocessor) into first-class [`Bid`](#bid) objects that can be ranked, simulated, and executed.

```typescript lineNumbers
buildBids(order: Order, bids: FillerBid[], sessionPrivateKey?: HexString): Bid[]
```

### sortBids(order, bids)

Sorts [`Bid`](#bid) objects by output value, using the same strategy the autopilot uses. Returns a new sorted array.

```typescript lineNumbers
async sortBids(order: Order, bids: Bid[]): Promise<Bid[]>
```

### selectAndExecuteBest(order, bids)

Autopilot bid selection over already-built [`Bid`](#bid) objects: sorts the bids, simulates each until one passes, then executes it.

```typescript lineNumbers
async selectAndExecuteBest(order: Order, bids: Bid[]): Promise<SelectBidResult>
```

### selectBid(order, bids, sessionPrivateKey?)

Legacy one-shot: decodes, sorts, simulates, signs, and submits the best of the given raw filler bids with no per-bid input from the caller. Prefer [`buildBids`](#buildbidsorder-bids-sessionprivatekey) + [`selectAndExecuteBest`](#selectandexecutebestorder-bids) (or [`executeBest`](#executebestorder-graffiti-options)) for new code.

```typescript lineNumbers
async selectBid(order: Order, bids: FillerBid[], sessionPrivateKey?: HexString): Promise<SelectBidResult>
```

### quoteUniswap(params)

> Standalone export (`import { quoteUniswap } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"`), not a method on `IntentGateway`.

Quotes a same-chain Uniswap swap that can be used when constructing the input or output side of an intent order. The helper checks Uniswap V2, V3, and V4 by default; pass `protocols: ["v4"]` to quote Uniswap V4 only.

```typescript lineNumbers
import { quoteUniswap } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const result = await quoteUniswap({
  chainId: 8453,
  tokenIn: {
    address: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    decimals: 6,
    symbol: "USDC",
    chainId: 8453,
  },
  tokenOut: {
    address: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    decimals: 18,
    symbol: "ETH",
    chainId: 8453,
  },
  amountIn: 100_000_000n,
  tradeType: "EXACT_INPUT",
  protocols: ["v4"],
})

console.log(result.bestQuote?.amountOut)
```

Set `recipient` to include executable transaction calldata in each quote. For exact-output swaps, use `tradeType: "EXACT_OUTPUT"` with `amountOut` instead of `amountIn`.

### cancelOrder(order, indexerClient, options?)

Async generator that cancels a placed order and streams status events until cancellation is complete. Supports both source-chain and destination-chain initiated cancellation.

```typescript lineNumbers
async *cancelOrder(
  order: Order,
  indexerClient: IsmpClient,
  options?: { from?: "source" | "destination" },
): AsyncGenerator<CancelEvent>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `order` | `Order` | — | The order to cancel |
| `indexerClient` | `IsmpClient` | — | Indexer client for streaming ISMP request status |
| `options` | `{ from?: "source" \| "destination" }` | `{}` | Pass `{ from: "destination" }` to initiate on the destination chain. |

**Yields:** `CancelEvent`

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const gen = gateway.cancelOrder(order, indexerClient)
for await (const event of gen) {
  switch (event.status) {
    case "DESTINATION_FINALIZED":
      console.log("Destination proof ready at height:", event.proof.height)
      break
    case "AWAITING_CANCEL_TRANSACTION": {
      // cancelOrder is a bidirectional generator — pass the signed tx or tx hash back.
      const txHash = await signer.sendTransaction({
        to: event.to,
        data: event.data,
        value: event.value,
      })
      // gen.next(txHash) resumes the generator; CANCEL_STARTED is consumed here.
      const { value: cancelStarted } = await gen.next(txHash)
      if (cancelStarted?.status === "CANCEL_STARTED") {
        console.log("Cancel tx confirmed:", cancelStarted.receipt.transactionHash)
      }
      break
    }
    case "SOURCE_FINALIZED":
      console.log("Cancel request finalised on source:", event.metadata.transactionHash)
      break
    case "HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED":
      console.log("Cancel message delivered to Hyperbridge:", event.metadata.transactionHash)
      break
    case "HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED":
      console.log("Cancel message finalised on Hyperbridge:", event.metadata.transactionHash)
      break
    case "CANCELLATION_COMPLETE":
      console.log("Refunded in tx:", event.transactionHash)
      break
  }
}
```

### cancelOrderFromSource(order, indexerClient)

### cancelOrderFromDest(order, indexerClient)

### orderStatusStream(commitment)

Streams status updates for an order as it progresses through placement, filling,
and redemption. Terminates when the order reaches a terminal state (`FILLED`,

```typescript lineNumbers
    }
  },

>
```

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers

}
```

## Types

### IntentOrderStatusUpdate

Tagged union of all status updates yielded by the `execute` generator. Use the `status` field to discriminate.

```typescript lineNumbers
type IntentOrderStatusUpdate =
  | { status: "AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER"; to: HexString; data: HexString; value?: bigint; sessionPrivateKey: HexString }
  | { status: "ORDER_PLACED"; order: Order; receipt: TransactionReceipt }
  | { status: "AWAITING_BIDS"; commitment: HexString; totalFilledAssets: TokenInfo[]; remainingAssets: TokenInfo[] }
  | { status: "NEW_BID"; commitment: HexString; bid: Bid }
  | { status: "BIDS_RECEIVED"; commitment: HexString; bidCount: number; bids: Bid[] }
  | { status: "BID_SELECTED"; commitment: HexString; selectedSolver: HexString; userOpHash: HexString; userOp: PackedUserOperation; transactionHash?: HexString }
  | { status: "FILLED"; commitment: HexString; userOpHash: HexString; selectedSolver: HexString; transactionHash?: HexString; totalFilledAssets: TokenInfo[]; remainingAssets: TokenInfo[] }
  | { status: "PARTIAL_FILL"; commitment: HexString; userOpHash: HexString; selectedSolver: HexString; transactionHash?: HexString; filledAssets: TokenInfo[]; totalFilledAssets: TokenInfo[]; remainingAssets: TokenInfo[] }
  | { status: "EXPIRED"; commitment: HexString; totalFilledAssets?: TokenInfo[]; remainingAssets?: TokenInfo[]; error: string }
  | { status: "FAILED"; commitment?: HexString; totalFilledAssets?: TokenInfo[]; remainingAssets?: TokenInfo[]; error: string }
```

| Status | Fields | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| `AWAITING_PLACE_ORDER` | `to`, `data`, `value?`, `sessionPrivateKey` | Caller must sign and broadcast the placement transaction, then send back the tx hash |
| `ORDER_PLACED` | `order`, `receipt` | Order confirmed on-chain; `receipt` is the full viem `TransactionReceipt` of the placement transaction |
| `AWAITING_BIDS` | `commitment`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets` | Polling the coprocessor for solver bids |
| `NEW_BID` | `commitment`, `bid` | A previously unseen bid arrived during the auction (informational; one [`Bid`](#bid)) |
| `BIDS_RECEIVED` | `commitment`, `bidCount`, `bids` | Auction round complete; `bids` is an array of executable [`Bid`](#bid) objects to select from |
| `BID_SELECTED` | `commitment`, `selectedSolver`, `userOpHash`, `userOp`, `transactionHash?` | Best bid selected and UserOperation submitted to the bundler |
| `FILLED` | `commitment`, `userOpHash`, `selectedSolver`, `transactionHash?`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets` | Order fully filled on the destination chain |
| `PARTIAL_FILL` | `commitment`, `userOpHash`, `selectedSolver`, `transactionHash?`, `filledAssets`, `totalFilledAssets`, `remainingAssets` | Order partially filled; more fills may follow |
| `EXPIRED` | `commitment`, `totalFilledAssets?`, `remainingAssets?`, `error` | Order deadline reached or no new bids available — terminal |
| `FAILED` | `commitment?`, `totalFilledAssets?`, `remainingAssets?`, `error` | Retryable error (e.g. bundler rejection, simulation failure) — executor retries automatically |

### Bid

A first-class, executable solver bid surfaced via the `NEW_BID` and `BIDS_RECEIVED` status updates. Each `Bid` wraps a single decoded `FillerBid` and exposes the metadata needed to rank it alongside the two primitives required to act on it: `simulate()` to pre-check it off-chain, and `execute()` to sign the solver selection and submit the UserOperation to the bundler.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface Bid {
  /** The solver account that submitted this bid (`userOp.sender`). */
  readonly solverAddress: HexString
  /** Decoded fill outputs — the tokens and amounts the solver offers. */
  readonly outputs: TokenInfo[]
  /** Relayer fee from the decoded fill options. */
  readonly relayerFee: bigint
  /** Hyperbridge native dispatch fee from the decoded fill options. */
  readonly nativeDispatchFee: bigint
  /** Raw UserOperation for advanced consumers (custom batching, paymaster flows). */
  readonly userOp: PackedUserOperation

  /** Runs the batched `select` + `fillOrder` `eth_call` simulation. Throws if it reverts. */
  simulate(): Promise<void>
  /** Signs the `SelectSolver` message, packs the signature, and submits the UserOp to the bundler. */
  execute(): Promise<SelectBidResult>
  /** Prices the bid's outputs in USD. Returns `null` when any output token cannot be priced. */
  outputUsdValue(): Promise<Decimal | null>
}
```

The session-key signature over the `SelectSolver` message is resolved lazily and cached, so it is signed at most once whether you call `simulate()`, `execute()`, or both.

### SelectBidResult

Returned by `Bid.execute()` (and the autopilot helpers). Fed back into the `execute` / `resume` generator after `BIDS_RECEIVED` so the executor can continue tracking fills.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface SelectBidResult {
  userOp: PackedUserOperation
  userOpHash: HexString
  solverAddress: HexString
  commitment: HexString
  /** Destination fill tx hash, once available. */
  txnHash?: HexString
  /** Fill outcome for same-chain orders, derived from on-chain logs. */
  fillStatus?: "full" | "partial"
  /** Assets filled in this UserOperation (best-effort, from `PartialFill` logs). */
  filledAssets?: TokenInfo[]
}
```

### CancelEvent

Tagged union of all status updates yielded by the `cancelOrder` generator.

```typescript lineNumbers
type BlockMetadata = {
  blockHash: string
  blockNumber: number
  transactionHash: string
  timestamp?: number
}

type CancelEvent =
  | { status: "DESTINATION_FINALIZED"; proof: IProof }
  | { status: "AWAITING_CANCEL_TRANSACTION"; data: HexString; to: HexString; value: bigint }
  | { status: "CANCEL_STARTED"; receipt: TransactionReceipt }
  | { status: "SOURCE_FINALIZED"; metadata: BlockMetadata }
  | { status: "HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED"; metadata: BlockMetadata }
  | { status: "HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED"; metadata: BlockMetadata }
  | { status: "CANCELLATION_COMPLETE"; blockNumber: number; transactionHash: HexString }
```

| Status | Fields | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| `DESTINATION_FINALIZED` | `proof` | State proof from the destination chain is ready |
| `AWAITING_CANCEL_TRANSACTION` | `data`, `to`, `value` | Caller must sign and submit the cancel transaction |
| `CANCEL_STARTED` | `receipt` | Cancel transaction confirmed on-chain |
| `SOURCE_FINALIZED` | `metadata` | Cancel request finalised on source chain |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED` | `metadata` | Cancel message delivered to Hyperbridge |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED` | `metadata` | Cancel message finalised on Hyperbridge |
| `CANCELLATION_COMPLETE` | `blockNumber`, `transactionHash` | Escrow refunded; cancellation done |

### Order

Represents a cross-chain swap intent submitted to IntentGatewayV2.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface Order {
  id?: string          // Order commitment hash (populated after placement)
  user: HexString      // Address of the order creator
  source: HexString    // State-machine ID of the source chain (e.g. "EVM-1")
  destination: HexString // State-machine ID of the destination chain (e.g. "EVM-42161")
  deadline: bigint     // Unix timestamp after which the order can be cancelled
  nonce: bigint        // Unique order nonce (set by contract on placement)
  fees: bigint         // Protocol fee in fee-token units
  session: HexString   // Ephemeral session key address (set during placement)
  predispatch: DispatchInfo // Optional calls to execute on the source chain before escrowing
  inputs: TokenInfo[]  // Tokens escrowed on the source chain
  output: PaymentInfo  // Token the solver must deliver on the destination chain
}
```

### TokenInfo

A token address and amount pair used in `Order` inputs.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface TokenInfo {
  token: HexString   // ERC-20 token contract address
  amount: bigint     // Token amount in the token's native decimals
}
```

### PaymentInfo

Describes the output the solver must deliver on the destination chain.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface PaymentInfo {
  beneficiary: HexString  // Address to receive the output tokens
  assets: TokenInfo[]     // Tokens the solver must deliver
  call: HexString         // Optional calldata to execute on the destination after fill
}
```

### DispatchInfo

Describes optional calls to execute on the source chain before inputs are escrowed.

```typescript lineNumbers
interface DispatchInfo {
  assets: TokenInfo[]  // Tokens consumed by the predispatch call
  call: HexString      // Calldata to execute before escrowing inputs
}
```

# IsmpClient

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/ismp-client.mdx

title: IsmpClient
description: API reference for the IsmpClient class - query the Hyperbridge indexer and monitor cross-chain request statuses.

# IsmpClient

The `IsmpClient` class provides methods for querying the Hyperbridge indexer and monitoring cross-chain request statuses in real-time.

## Constructor

### new IsmpClient(config)

Creates a new IsmpClient instance.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `config.queryClient` | `QueryClient` | Query client instance for the Hyperbridge indexer |
| `config.pollInterval` | `number` | Polling interval in milliseconds (default: 1000) |
| `config.source` | `IChain` | Source chain instance (EvmChain or SubstrateChain) |
| `config.dest` | `IChain` | Destination chain instance (EvmChain or SubstrateChain) |
| `config.hyperbridge` | `IChain` | Hyperbridge chain instance (typically SubstrateChain) |

**Returns:** `IsmpClient`

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const indexer = new IsmpClient({
  queryClient: createQueryClient({ url: "https://indexer-url" }),
  pollInterval: 1_000,
  source: sourceChain,
  dest: destChain,
  hyperbridge: hyperbridgeChain
})
```

## Instance Methods

### postRequestStatusStream(hash)

Creates an async generator that streams status updates for a POST request. The stream automatically monitors both request progress and timeout events. Terminates when the request reaches a terminal state (DESTINATION or PENDING_TIMEOUT).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `hash` | `HexString` | Request commitment hash, or transaction hash from any chain in the request lifecycle |

**Returns:** `AsyncGenerator<RequestStatusWithMetadata, void>`

**Yields:**

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `RequestStatus.SOURCE` | Request dispatched from source chain |
| `RequestStatus.SOURCE_FINALIZED` | Request finalized on source chain |
| `RequestStatus.HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED` | Request delivered to Hyperbridge |
| `RequestStatus.HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED` | Request finalized on Hyperbridge |
| `RequestStatus.DESTINATION` | Request executed on destination chain (terminal) |
| `TimeoutStatus.PENDING_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded timeout period (terminal) |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
for await (const status of indexer.postRequestStatusStream(requestHash)) {
  console.log(`Status: ${status.status}`)
  console.log(`Block: ${status.metadata.blockNumber}`)
  console.log(`TX: ${status.metadata.transactionHash}`)
  
  if (status.status === "DESTINATION" || status.status === "PENDING_TIMEOUT") {
    break
  }
}
```

### getRequestStatusStream(hash)

Creates an async generator that streams status updates for a GET request. Terminates when the request reaches a terminal state.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `hash` | `HexString` | Request commitment hash, or transaction hash from any chain in the request lifecycle |

**Returns:** `AsyncGenerator<RequestStatusWithMetadata, void>`

**Yields:** Same status types as `postRequestStatusStream()`

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
for await (const status of indexer.getRequestStatusStream(requestHash)) {
  console.log(`GET Request Status: ${status.status}`)
  
  if (status.status === "DESTINATION" || status.status === "PENDING_TIMEOUT") {
    break
  }
}
```

### postRequestTimeoutStream(hash)

Creates an async generator that streams timeout processing status updates for a POST request. Use this method when `postRequestStatusStream()` yields `TimeoutStatus.PENDING_TIMEOUT`.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `hash` | `HexString` | Request commitment hash |

**Returns:** `AsyncGenerator<PostRequestTimeoutStatus, void>`

**Yields:**

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `TimeoutStatus.PENDING_TIMEOUT` | Request has exceeded timeout period |
| `TimeoutStatus.DESTINATION_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT` | Timeout finalized on destination |
| `TimeoutStatus.HYPERBRIDGE_TIMED_OUT` | Timeout message delivered to Hyperbridge |
| `TimeoutStatus.HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT` | Timeout finalized on Hyperbridge |
| `TimeoutStatus.TIMED_OUT` | Timeout finalized on source chain (terminal) |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
// After receiving PENDING_TIMEOUT status
for await (const status of indexer.postRequestTimeoutStream(requestHash)) {
  console.log(`Timeout Status: ${status.status}`)
  
  if (status.status === "TIMED_OUT") {
    console.log("Request timeout complete")
    break
  }
}
```

### getRequestTimeoutStream(hash)

Creates an async generator that streams timeout processing status updates for a GET request.

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `hash` | `HexString` | Request commitment hash |

**Returns:** `AsyncGenerator<PostRequestTimeoutStatus, void>`

**Yields:** Same status types as `postRequestTimeoutStream()`

### queryRequestWithStatus(commitment)

Queries the current status of a request without streaming.

**Parameters:**

## Usage Notes

### Stream Lifecycle

- Async generators created by stream methods must be properly terminated
- Always break out of loops when a terminal status is reached
- Use `for await...of` loops or manual iteration with `.next()`
- Streams automatically poll at the configured `pollInterval`

### Terminal States

**Request Status Streams:**
- `RequestStatus.DESTINATION` - Request successfully executed
- `TimeoutStatus.PENDING_TIMEOUT` - Request timed out (switch to timeout stream)

**Timeout Status Streams:**
- `TimeoutStatus.TIMED_OUT` - Timeout processing complete

### Error Handling

Stream methods may throw errors for:
- Network connectivity issues
- Invalid commitment hashes
- Chain RPC failures

Implement try-catch blocks around stream iterations to handle errors gracefully.

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
try {
  for await (const status of indexer.postRequestStatusStream(hash)) {
    console.log(status)
    if (status.status === "DESTINATION") break
  }
} catch (error) {
  console.error("Stream error:", error)
  // Handle error appropriately
}
```

### Hash Resolution

All stream methods accept multiple hash types:
- Request commitment hash
- Source chain transaction hash
- Hyperbridge transaction hash
- Destination chain transaction hash
- Timeout transaction hash

The indexer automatically resolves the hash to the corresponding request.

## Related

- [Tracking Requests](/developers/sdk/tracking/post-requests) - Detailed guide on tracking request lifecycles
- [Getting Started](/developers/sdk/getting-started) - Initialize IsmpClient

# SubstrateChain

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/substrate-chain.mdx

title: SubstrateChain
description: API reference for SubstrateChain - interact with Substrate-based chains in the Hyperbridge protocol.

# SubstrateChain

The `SubstrateChain` class provides methods for interacting with Substrate-based chains (Polkadot parachains, including Hyperbridge) in the Hyperbridge protocol. It handles MMR proof generation, child trie queries, and cross-chain message verification.

```typescript lineNumbers
class SubstrateChain implements IChain
```

## Static Methods

### SubstrateChain.connect(params)

Creates a new `SubstrateChain` instance and immediately establishes the WebSocket connection, returning a fully initialised chain client. This is the preferred way to create a `SubstrateChain`.

```typescript lineNumbers
static async connect(params: ISubstrateConfig): Promise<SubstrateChain>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `params.stateMachineId` | `string` | State machine identifier (e.g., "POLKADOT-3367") |
| `params.wsUrl` | `string` | WebSocket URL for the Substrate node (must be an archive node) |
| `params.consensusStateId` | `string` | Consensus state identifier on Hyperbridge |
| `params.hasher` | `"Blake2" \| "Keccak"` | Hashing algorithm used by the chain |

**Returns:** `Promise<SubstrateChain>` — a connected chain instance, ready to use.

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { SubstrateChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const hyperbridge = await SubstrateChain.connect({
  stateMachineId: "POLKADOT-3367",
  wsUrl: "wss://hyperbridge-rpc.polkadot.io",
  consensusStateId: "DOT0",
  hasher: "Keccak"
})
```

## Properties

### api

The Polkadot.js API instance for interacting with the Substrate chain.

**Type:** `ApiPromise | undefined`

**Note:** Only available after connecting (via `SubstrateChain.connect(params)` or `instance.connect()`)

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
const chain = await SubstrateChain.connect({ /* ... */ })
const blockHash = await chain.api?.rpc.chain.getBlockHash()
```

### config

Returns the chain configuration object.

**Type:** `ISubstrateConfig`

**Returns:**

```typescript lineNumbers
{
  wsUrl: string
  consensusStateId: string
  hasher: "Blake2" | "Keccak"
  stateMachineId: string
}
```

## Important Notes

### Connection Management

Use `SubstrateChain.connect(params)` to create and connect in one step. The Polkadot.js API must be initialised before calling any query methods.

```typescript lineNumbers
const chain = await SubstrateChain.connect(config)

// Now you can use the chain
const timestamp = await chain.timestamp()

// Clean up when done
await chain.disconnect()
```

### Archive Node Requirement

The WebSocket URL must point to an archive node. Regular nodes only retain recent state and cannot provide:
- Historical storage proofs
- Child trie queries for older blocks
- MMR proofs for timeout scenarios

### Child Trie Storage

Substrate chains store ISMP data in a child trie named "ISMP". This provides isolated storage for:
- Request commitments
- Request receipts
- Response data

All ISMP-related queries go through the child trie storage system.

### Hasher Configuration

The `hasher` parameter specifies the hashing algorithm:
- **Keccak** - Used by Hyperbridge (Nexus, Gargantua)
- **Blake2** - Default for most Substrate chains

Using the wrong hasher will cause proof verification failures.

## Usage Example

```typescript lineNumbers
import { SubstrateChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// Create and connect to Hyperbridge
const hyperbridge = await SubstrateChain.connect({
  stateMachineId: "POLKADOT-3367",
  wsUrl: "wss://hyperbridge-rpc.polkadot.io",
  consensusStateId: "DOT0",
  hasher: "Keccak"
})

try {
  // Query current timestamp
  const time = await hyperbridge.timestamp()
  console.log(`Current time: ${time}`)
  
  // Check if a request was delivered
  const receipt = await hyperbridge.queryRequestReceipt(commitmentHash)
  if (receipt) {
    console.log(`Delivered by: ${receipt}`)
  }
  
  // Get latest state machine height
  const height = await hyperbridge.latestStateMachineHeight({
    stateId: { Ethereum: 1 }
  })
  console.log(`Latest Ethereum height: ${height}`)
  
} finally {
  // Always disconnect when done
  await hyperbridge.disconnect()
}
```

# TokenGateway (Deprecated)

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/api/token-gateway.mdx

title: TokenGateway (Deprecated)
description: API reference for TokenGateway — deprecated in favor of HyperFungibleToken.

# TokenGateway (Deprecated)

<Callout type="warn">
**TokenGateway has been deprecated.** The on-chain TokenGateway contracts have been replaced by
[HyperFungibleToken](/developers/polkadot/hyper-fungible-token) — a token that is itself a bridge
application, with no governance overhead or shared custody pool. The SDK class below will be
updated in a future release.
</Callout>

The `TokenGateway` class wraps the on-chain TokenGateway contract and provides
utilities for estimating the native-token cost of a cross-chain teleport, plus
(when configured with an indexer) snapshot queries and live streams of a
teleport's status.

Supports both EVM and Substrate chains as destination.

## Constructor

### new TokenGateway(params)

```typescript lineNumbers
new TokenGateway(params: { source: EvmChain; dest: EvmChain | SubstrateChain })
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `params.source` | `EvmChain` | Source EVM chain the teleport is dispatched from |
| `params.dest` | `EvmChain \| SubstrateChain` | Destination chain the asset is delivered to |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { TokenGateway, EvmChain, SubstrateChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const source = EvmChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 97,
  rpcUrl: "https://data-seed-prebsc-1-s1.binance.org:8545",
  host: "0x...",
  consensusStateId: "BSC0",
})
const dest = EvmChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 10200,
  rpcUrl: "https://rpc.chiadochain.net",
  host: "0x...",
  consensusStateId: "GNO0",
})

const tokenGateway = new TokenGateway({ source, dest })
```

## Methods

### quote(params)

Estimates the native-token cost of a teleport: relayer fee (for EVM
destinations — automatically estimated from gas on the destination chain plus
a 1% buffer) plus the Hyperbridge protocol fee (with a 1% buffer). Also returns
the relayer fee converted into the source chain's fee-token denomination via
the source-chain Uniswap V2 router.

Returns `0` relayer fee for non-EVM destinations.

```typescript lineNumbers
async quote(params: TeleportParams): Promise<QuoteNativeResult>
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `params.amount` | `bigint` | Amount to teleport |
| `params.assetId` | `HexString` | Asset identifier (e.g. `keccak256(toHex("USDC"))`) |
| `params.redeem` | `boolean` | Whether to redeem the underlying ERC-20 on the destination |
| `params.to` | `HexString` | Recipient address (32-byte) |
| `params.dest` | `string \| Uint8Array` | Destination state-machine ID |
| `params.timeout` | `bigint` | Request timeout in seconds |
| `params.data` | `HexString \| Uint8Array` | Optional destination contract calldata |

**Returns:** `Promise<QuoteNativeResult>`

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `totalNativeCost` | `bigint` | Total native-token cost (relayer + protocol fee, with 1% buffer) |
| `relayerFeeInSourceFeeToken` | `bigint` | Relayer fee converted to the source chain's fee token |

### withQueryClient(queryClient, options?)

Attaches a Hyperbridge indexer GraphQL client to this `TokenGateway` so that
[`queryAssetTeleported`](#queryassetteleportedcommitment) and
[`assetTeleportedStatusStream`](#assetteleportedstatusstreamcommitment) become
available. Returns `this` for chaining.

```typescript lineNumbers
withQueryClient(
  queryClient: IndexerQueryClient,
  options?: { pollInterval?: number; tracing?: boolean },
): this
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `queryClient` | `IndexerQueryClient` | GraphQL client from `createQueryClient(...)` |
| `options.pollInterval` | `number` | Poll interval in milliseconds (default: `1_000`) |
| `options.tracing` | `boolean` | Enable trace-level logging (default: `false`) |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
import { createQueryClient } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const queryClient = createQueryClient({ url: "https://indexer-url" })
const tokenGateway = new TokenGateway({ source, dest }).withQueryClient(queryClient)
```

### queryAssetTeleported(commitment)

Queries an asset-teleported event by commitment hash from the Hyperbridge
indexer.

Requires a prior call to [`withQueryClient`](#withqueryclientqueryclient-options).

```typescript lineNumbers
async queryAssetTeleported(commitment: HexString): Promise<TokenGatewayAssetTeleportedWithStatus | undefined>
```

### assetTeleportedStatusStream(commitment)

Streams status updates for an asset-teleported event until it reaches a
terminal state (`RECEIVED` or `REFUNDED`).

Requires a prior call to [`withQueryClient`](#withqueryclientqueryclient-options).

```typescript lineNumbers
async *assetTeleportedStatusStream(commitment: HexString): AsyncGenerator<
  {
    status: TeleportStatus
    metadata: {
      blockHash: string
      blockNumber: number
      transactionHash: string
      timestamp: bigint
    }
  },
  void
>
```

**Yields:**

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `TELEPORTED` | Teleport dispatched on the source chain |
| `RECEIVED` | Asset delivered on the destination chain (terminal) |
| `REFUNDED` | Teleport timed out and was refunded (terminal) |

**Example:**

```typescript lineNumbers
for await (const update of tokenGateway.assetTeleportedStatusStream(commitment)) {
  console.log(`Teleport status: ${update.status}`)
  if (["RECEIVED", "REFUNDED"].includes(update.status)) break
}
```

# Getting Started

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/getting-started.mdx

title: Getting Started
description: Quick start guide for initializing the Hyperbridge SDK and creating your first cross-chain connection.

# Getting Started

This guide will walk you through setting up the Hyperbridge SDK and creating your first cross-chain connection.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

- Node.js 22+ installed
- Basic knowledge of TypeScript/JavaScript
- RPC endpoints for your source and destination chains

## Installation

Install the SDK using your preferred package manager:

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'yarn', 'npm']}>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash lineNumbers
npm install @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash lineNumbers
yarn add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash lineNumbers
pnpm add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

**Using Vite?** If you're using Vite, you'll need to add the Hyperbridge Vite plugin to handle WebAssembly dependencies. See the [Vite Integration guide](/developers/sdk/vite-integration) for setup instructions.

## Quick Setup

### 1. Create Chain Instances

**EVM Chain:**

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { EvmChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// EvmChain.create() auto-detects the chain ID and resolves the IsmpHost address
const sourceChain = await EvmChain.create("https://data-seed-prebsc-1-s1.binance.org:8545")
```

**Substrate Chain:**

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { SubstrateChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const hyperbridge = await SubstrateChain.connect({
  stateMachineId: "KUSAMA-4009",
  wsUrl: "wss://gargantua.polytope.technology",
  hasher: "Keccak",
  consensusStateId: "PAS0"
})
```

**Polkadot Hub chain (EVM on Substrate / Revive):**

Use `PolkadotHubChain` when the execution environment is the EVM hosted on a Substrate chain (Revive). It wraps an internal [`EvmChain`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain) for RPC reads, contract calls, and transaction helpers, and uses a **Substrate JSON-RPC** endpoint to build storage proofs (`queryProof`, `queryStateProof`) from the main trie and Revive child tries—the same layout the relayer uses for Substrate-EVM.

`PolkadotHubChain.create(evmRpcUrl, substrateRpcUrl, bundlerUrl?)` mirrors [`EvmChain.create`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain): it resolves chain id and `IsmpHost` from known deployments, attaches your Substrate endpoint for proofs, and optionally forwards an ERC-4337 **bundler URL** as the third argument (same semantics as `EvmChain.create`).

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { PolkadotHubChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const evmRpc = "https://your-evm-endpoint.example"
const substrateRpc = "https://your-substrate-endpoint.example"

// Without a bundler (two arguments)
const polkadotHub = await PolkadotHubChain.create(evmRpc, substrateRpc)

// With an ERC-4337 bundler (optional third argument, same as EvmChain.create)
const polkadotHubWithBundler = await PolkadotHubChain.create(
  evmRpc,
  substrateRpc,
  "https://your-bundler.example",
)
```

Or pass full parameters when you already know chain id and host:

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { PolkadotHubChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const polkadotHub = PolkadotHubChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 420420417,
  rpcUrl: "https://your-evm-endpoint.example",
  host: "0xYourIsmpHostAddress",
  substrateRpcUrl: "https://your-substrate-endpoint.example",
  // Optional — defaults exist for some known chain IDs (same as EvmChain)
  consensusStateId: "PAS0",
  // Optional — ERC-4337 bundler, same as EvmChain
  // bundlerUrl: "https://...",
})
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `chainId`, `rpcUrl`, `host` | Same as [`EvmChain`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain): EVM chain id, JSON-RPC URL, and `IsmpHost` address. |
| `substrateRpcUrl` | Substrate node RPC (HTTP or WebSocket). WebSocket URLs are converted to HTTP for proof RPCs. |
| `consensusStateId` | Optional Hyperbridge consensus state id for this chain (mirrors `EvmChain`). |
| `bundlerUrl` | Optional account-abstraction bundler (mirrors `EvmChain`). |

The instance’s `config` includes every `IEvmConfig` field plus `substrateRpcUrl` (`IPolkadotHubConfig`).

**Proofs:** `queryProof` **must** be called with an explicit finalized (or chosen) block height as `at`. Other `IChain` methods delegate to the inner EVM client, same pattern as other chain types.

**Pharos chain:**

Use `PharosChain` when connecting to a Pharos network. Pharos exposes a standard EVM JSON-RPC surface, but its `eth_getProof` endpoint returns proofs in a custom hexary hash tree format (SHA-256) instead of Ethereum's Merkle-Patricia Trie (Keccak-256). `PharosChain` wraps an internal [`EvmChain`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain) for all standard interactions and overrides `queryProof` / `queryStateProof` to handle the Pharos proof format.

`PharosChain.create(rpcUrl, bundlerUrl?)` mirrors [`EvmChain.create`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain): it resolves chain id and `IsmpHost` from known deployments, and optionally forwards an ERC-4337 **bundler URL** as the second argument.

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { PharosChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// Auto-detect chain ID and IsmpHost from the RPC
const pharos = await PharosChain.create("https://rpc.pharos.example")

// With an ERC-4337 bundler (optional second argument, same as EvmChain.create)
const pharosWithBundler = await PharosChain.create(
  "https://rpc.pharos.example",
  "https://your-bundler.example",
)
```

Or pass full parameters when you already know chain id and host:

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { PharosChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const pharos = PharosChain.fromParams({
  chainId: 688689,
  rpcUrl: "https://rpc.pharos-atlantic.example",
  host: "0xYourIsmpHostAddress",
  // Optional — defaults exist for some known chain IDs (same as EvmChain)
  // consensusStateId: "PHAR",
  // Optional — ERC-4337 bundler, same as EvmChain
  // bundlerUrl: "https://...",
})
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `chainId`, `rpcUrl`, `host` | Same as [`EvmChain`](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain): EVM chain id, JSON-RPC URL, and `IsmpHost` address. |
| `consensusStateId` | Optional Hyperbridge consensus state id for this chain (mirrors `EvmChain`). |
| `bundlerUrl` | Optional account-abstraction bundler (mirrors `EvmChain`). |

**Proofs:** `queryProof` **must** be called with an explicit finalized block height as `at`. The returned proof is a SCALE-encoded `PharosStateProof` containing hexary hash tree proof nodes, storage values, non-existence proofs, and account proofs. Other `IChain` methods delegate to the inner EVM client.

| Chain | Chain ID |
|-------|----------|
| Pharos Mainnet | 688600 |
| Pharos Atlantic (Testnet) | 688689 |

For detailed configuration options and supported chains, see:
- [EvmChain API Reference](/developers/sdk/api/evm-chain) (shared EVM surface for Polkadot Hub and Pharos)
- [SubstrateChain API Reference](/developers/sdk/api/substrate-chain)

### 2. Create Query Client

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { createQueryClient } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const queryClient = createQueryClient({
  url: "https://gargantua.indexer.polytope.technology"
})
```

Polytope Labs provides a free indexer service for both mainnet and testnet. The endpoints are actually GraphQL APIs, so a GraphiQL playground is available at the endpoints as well.

| Network | Indexer URL |
|---------|-------------|
| Mainnet | https://nexus.indexer.polytope.technology |
| Testnet | https://gargantua.indexer.polytope.technology |

### 3. Initialize IsmpClient

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { IsmpClient } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const indexer = new IsmpClient({
  queryClient,
  pollInterval: 1_000, // Poll every 1 second
  source: sourceChain,
  dest: destChain,
  hyperbridge: hyperbridge
})
```

**Configuration Options:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `queryClient` | `QueryClient` | Query client for the Hyperbridge indexer |
| `pollInterval` | `number` | Polling interval in milliseconds (default: 1000) |
| `source` | `IChain` | Source chain instance (`EvmChain`, `SubstrateChain`, `PolkadotHubChain`, `PharosChain`, …) |
| `dest` | `IChain` | Destination chain instance |
| `hyperbridge` | `IChain` | Hyperbridge chain instance (often `SubstrateChain`) |

For complete API documentation and usage examples, see the [IsmpClient API Reference](/developers/sdk/api/ismp-client).

## Complete Example

```typescript lineNumbers title="client.ts" icon=typescript
import { 
  IsmpClient, 
  createQueryClient, 
  EvmChain,
  SubstrateChain 
} from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

async function main() {
  // 1. Create query client
  const queryClient = createQueryClient({
    url: "https://gargantua.indexer.polytope.technology"
  })

  // 2. Create chain instances — auto-detects chain ID and IsmpHost address
  const sourceChain = await EvmChain.create("https://data-seed-prebsc-1-s1.binance.org:8545")
  const destChain   = await EvmChain.create("https://rpc.chiadochain.net")

  const hyperbridgeChain = await SubstrateChain.connect({
    stateMachineId: "KUSAMA-4009",
    wsUrl: "wss://gargantua.polytope.technology",
    hasher: "Keccak",
    consensusStateId: "PAS0"
  })

  // 3. Initialize IsmpClient
  const indexer = new IsmpClient({
    queryClient,
    pollInterval: 1_000,
    source: sourceChain,
    dest: destChain,
    hyperbridge: hyperbridgeChain
  })

  console.log("✓ SDK initialized successfully!")

  // 4. Track a request (example)
  const requestHash = "0xYourRequestHashHere"
  
  for await (const status of indexer.postRequestStatusStream(requestHash)) {
    console.log(`Status: ${status.status}`)
    
    if (status.status === "DESTINATION" || status.status === "PENDING_TIMEOUT") {
      break
    }
  }
  
  // Clean up
  await hyperbridgeChain.disconnect()
}

main().catch(console.error)
```

# Bridging Tokens with HyperFungibleToken

Source: https://github.com/polytope-labs/hyperbridge/blob/main/docs/content/developers/sdk/hyper-fungible-token.mdx

title: Hyper Fungible Token
description: Guide for bridging tokens cross-chain using the HyperFungibleToken SDK class.

# Bridging Tokens with HyperFungibleToken

This guide walks through bridging ERC20 tokens cross-chain using the `HyperFungibleToken` SDK class. The class supports both `HyperFungibleToken` (burn/mint) and `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` (lock/unlock) contracts, with automatic type detection via ERC165.

## Overview

`HyperFungibleToken` replaces the deprecated [TokenGateway](/developers/sdk/api/token-gateway). TokenGateway required a shared custody pool across all tokens, a token-governor contract for cross-chain governance, and a token-gateway-inspector for validation — all of which added significant operational overhead and created a single point of failure for all bridged assets. With HyperFungibleToken, each token is its own self-contained bridge application, eliminating shared custody risk and governance complexity entirely.

The typical architecture deploys a `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` on the token's home chain (locking the canonical ERC20 supply) and a `HyperFungibleToken` on every remote chain (minting/burning). See the [EVM contract guide](/developers/evm/hyper-fungible-token) for deployment details.

The SDK class abstracts over both contract types — it detects the type via ERC165 and handles approvals, fee quoting, and transaction building automatically.

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step>
### Install the SDK

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'yarn', 'npm']}>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash
pnpm add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash
yarn add @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash
npm install @hyperbridge/sdk
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
<Step>
### Create chain instances

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import { EvmChain } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

// EvmChain.create auto-detects chain ID and resolves the IsmpHost address
const source = await EvmChain.create("https://data-seed-prebsc-1-s1.binance.org:8545")
const dest = await EvmChain.create("https://rpc-amoy.polygon.technology")
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Create the HyperFungibleToken instance

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import { HyperFungibleToken } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const hft = new HyperFungibleToken({ source, dest })
```
</Step>
</Steps>

## Quoting Fees

Before bridging, quote the fee to determine the cost:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import { parseEther } from "viem"

const fee = await hft.quote({
  token: "0x...",           // HFT or WrappedHFT contract address
  from: senderAddress,
  to: recipientAddress,
  amount: parseEther("100"),
  dest: "EVM-80002",
})

console.log(fee.totalNativeCost)       // msg.value if paying in native
console.log(fee.totalFeeTokenCost)     // cost if paying in fee token
console.log(fee.relayerFeeInFeeToken)  // relayer fee component
```

The fee estimation pipeline estimates gas for delivering the message on the destination chain, converts the destination gas cost to the destination fee token via Uniswap, scales decimals between source and destination fee tokens, then calls the on-chain `quote()` and `quote()` methods to get the final cost.

<Callout type="info">
`totalNativeCost` may be `0n` on chains without a Uniswap router. In this case, use `payInFeeToken: true` when bridging.
</Callout>

## Bridging Tokens

The `bridge()` method returns an async generator that yields steps for the caller to execute. This design gives the caller full control over transaction signing and submission.

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http, parseEther } from "viem"
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts"
import { bscTestnet } from "viem/chains"

const account = privateKeyToAccount(PRIVATE_KEY)
const walletClient = createWalletClient({
  account,
  chain: bscTestnet,
  transport: http(BSC_RPC),
})
const publicClient = createPublicClient({
  chain: bscTestnet,
  transport: http(BSC_RPC),
})

const gen = hft.bridge({
  token: "0x...",
  from: account.address,
  to: recipientAddress,
  amount: parseEther("1"),
  dest: "EVM-80002",
  timeout: 3600n,          // 1 hour
  payInFeeToken: true,     // pay in fee token instead of native
})

let result = await gen.next()

while (!result.done) {
  const step = result.value
  if (!step) break

  if (step.type === "approve") {
    const hash = await walletClient.sendTransaction({
      to: step.tx.to,
      data: step.tx.data,
    })
    await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })
    result = await gen.next()
    continue
  }

  if (step.type === "send") {
    const hash = await walletClient.sendTransaction({
      to: step.tx.to,
      data: step.tx.data,
      value: step.tx.value,
    })
    result = await gen.next(hash) // resume with tx hash
    continue
  }

  if (step.type === "submitted") {
    console.log("Commitment:", step.commitment)
    result = await gen.next()
    continue
  }

  result = await gen.next()
}
```

### Generator Steps

The generator yields these steps in order:

| Step | When | What to do |
|------|------|------------|
| `approve` | WrappedHFT (underlying ERC20 approval) or `payInFeeToken: true` (fee token approval). Only if current allowance is insufficient. | Submit the approval tx, wait for receipt, call `gen.next()` |
| `send` | Always | Submit the send tx, call `gen.next(txHash)` with the hash |
| `submitted` | After send is mined | Read `step.commitment` — the ISMP request commitment hash |
| `status` | Only if `client` was provided | Track the cross-chain lifecycle |

## Tracking Cross-Chain Status

To receive status updates after the transaction is submitted, provide an `IsmpClient`:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import {
  IsmpClient,
  createQueryClient,
  SubstrateChain,
  HyperFungibleToken,
} from "@hyperbridge/sdk"

const hyperbridge = await SubstrateChain.connect({
  wsUrl: "wss://gargantua.rpc.polytope.technology",
  consensusStateId: "PAS0",
  hasher: "Keccak",
  stateMachineId: "KUSAMA-4009",
})

const queryClient = createQueryClient({
  url: "https://gargantua.indexer.polytope.technology",
})

const ismpClient = new IsmpClient({
  queryClient,
  source,
  dest,
  hyperbridge,
  pollInterval: 5_000,
})

const hft = new HyperFungibleToken({ source, dest, client: ismpClient })
```

With `client` attached, the generator yields `status` steps after `submitted`:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
if (step.type === "status") {
  console.log(`Status: ${step.status}`)

  if (step.status === "DESTINATION" || step.status === "TIMED_OUT") {
    break
  }

  result = await gen.next()
  continue
}
```

The status progression is:

```
SOURCE_FINALIZED → HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED → HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED → DESTINATION
```

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `SOURCE_FINALIZED` | The source chain transaction has been finalized |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_DELIVERED` | Hyperbridge has received and verified the message |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED` | Hyperbridge has produced a proof for the destination chain. Metadata includes `calldata` for self-relay. |
| `DESTINATION` | The message has been delivered on the destination chain |
| `TIMED_OUT` | The request timed out without being delivered |

### Tracking independently

If you prefer not to pass `client` to the `HyperFungibleToken` constructor, you can track the request separately using the commitment from the `submitted` step:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
const hft = new HyperFungibleToken({ source, dest }) // no client

// ... run bridge generator, capture commitment from "submitted" step ...

for await (const status of ismpClient.postRequestStatusStream(commitment)) {
  console.log(`Status: ${status.status}`)
  if (status.status === "DESTINATION" || status.status === "TIMED_OUT") break
}
```

This is useful when you want to decouple the bridge transaction from status tracking — for example, submitting the transaction in one process and monitoring it in another.

## Handling Timeouts

If a cross-chain transfer is not delivered before its `timeout` expires, the tokens are not automatically refunded. The developer must initiate the timeout flow to recover the locked/burned tokens.

The bridge generator's status stream will detect when a request has timed out:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
if (step.type === "status") {
  if (step.status === "TIMED_OUT") {
    console.log("Request timed out — initiate timeout recovery")
    break
  }
}
```

After detecting the timeout, the developer must start a separate timeout stream using the `IsmpClient` to track the timeout proof as it propagates through Hyperbridge back to the source chain:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import { TimeoutStatus } from "@hyperbridge/sdk"
import EVM_HOST from "@hyperbridge/sdk/abis/evmHost"

// commitment was captured from the "submitted" step earlier
for await (const timeout of ismpClient.postRequestTimeoutStream(commitment)) {
  console.log(`Timeout status: ${timeout.status}`)

  if (timeout.status === TimeoutStatus.HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT) {
    // The timeout proof is ready — submit it to the source chain handler
    const hostParams = await sourcePublicClient.readContract({
      address: SOURCE_HOST_ADDRESS,
      abi: EVM_HOST.ABI,
      functionName: "hostParams",
    })

    const hash = await sourceWalletClient.sendTransaction({
      to: hostParams.handler,
      data: timeout.metadata.calldata,
    })
    await sourcePublicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })
    console.log("Timeout executed — tokens refunded")
  }

  if (timeout.status === TimeoutStatus.TIMED_OUT) break
}
```

### Timeout Lifecycle

The timeout flow progresses through these stages:

```
PENDING_TIMEOUT → DESTINATION_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT → HYPERBRIDGE_TIMED_OUT → HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT → TIMED_OUT
```

| Stage | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `PENDING_TIMEOUT` | Request has exceeded its timeout period |
| `DESTINATION_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT` | Destination chain finalized a block past the timeout |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_TIMED_OUT` | Timeout processed on Hyperbridge, request deleted from state |
| `HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED_TIMEOUT` | Hyperbridge finalized the timeout proof. Metadata includes `calldata` to submit to the source chain. |
| `TIMED_OUT` | Timeout transaction executed on source chain — tokens refunded |

When the timeout is executed on-chain:
- **HyperFungibleToken**: re-mints the burned tokens to the original sender
- **WrappedHyperFungibleToken**: transfers the locked underlying ERC20 back. For WETH, unwraps and sends native ETH.

<Callout type="info">
Timeout calldata is submitted to the **source** chain handler (not the destination), since the refund happens on the source chain where the tokens were burned or locked.
</Callout>

For the full timeout tracking reference, see [POST Request Timeouts](/developers/sdk/tracking/timeouts).

## Self-Relay

When `relayerFee` is set to `0n`, no relayer will deliver the message. Instead, extract the proof calldata from the `HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED` status and submit it to the destination chain yourself:

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
import EVM_HOST from "@hyperbridge/sdk/abis/evmHost"

const gen = hft.bridge({
  token: "0x...",
  from: account.address,
  to: account.address,
  amount: parseEther("1"),
  dest: "EVM-80002",
  relayerFee: 0n,           // no relayer fee — self-relay
  payInFeeToken: true,
})

// ... handle approve/send/submitted steps ...

if (step.type === "status" && step.status === "HYPERBRIDGE_FINALIZED") {
  const { calldata } = step.metadata

  // Read the handler address from the destination host contract
  const hostParams = await destPublicClient.readContract({
    address: DEST_HOST_ADDRESS,
    abi: EVM_HOST.ABI,
    functionName: "hostParams",
  })

  // Submit the proof to the destination chain
  const hash = await destWalletClient.sendTransaction({
    to: hostParams.handler,
    data: calldata,
  })
  await destPublicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })
}
```

This is useful for testing, for applications that want to guarantee delivery without relayer dependency, or for reducing costs by avoiding relayer fees.

## Detecting Token Type

To check whether a token contract is a `WrappedHyperFungibleToken` (lock/unlock) or a `HyperFungibleToken` (burn/mint):

```typescript lineNumbers title="bridge.ts" icon=typescript
const isWrapped = await hft.isWrapped(tokenAddress)
// true  → WrappedHyperFungibleToken (lock/unlock)
// false → HyperFungibleToken (burn/mint) or non-HFT contract
```

This uses ERC165 `supportsInterface` with interface ID `0xe23d9765`.

# Typescript Developers

The `@hyperbridge/sdk` is a comprehensive TypeScript SDK that provides utilities for interacting with the Hyperbridge indexer, monitoring cross-chain message statuses, and managing chain interactions. It supports both EVM and Substrate chains, offering a unified interface for tracking POST and GET requests across different blockchain networks.

## Overview

The SDK consists of several key components that work together to provide a seamless cross-chain development experience:

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **IsmpClient** | Main client for querying the Hyperbridge indexer and monitoring request statuses |
| **EvmChain** | Implementation for EVM-compatible chains |
| **SubstrateChain** | Implementation for Substrate-based chains |

- **[Getting Started](/developers/sdk/getting-started)** - Initialize the SDK and create your first cross-chain connection

- **[Tracking Requests](/developers/sdk/tracking/post-requests)** - Track POST and GET requests throughout their lifecycle
